title.zh: 卷五十 志第四十 兵
title.raw: 卷五十 志第四十 兵 Volume 50 Treatises 46: Military

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 古之有天下國家者，其興亡治亂，未始不以德，而自戰國、秦、漢以來，鮮不以兵。

translations.literal: From antiquity, those who possessed the realm and a state—in their rise and fall, order and disorder—never failed to depend on virtue; yet from the Warring States, Qin, and Han onward, rarely did they not rely on arms.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, the rise and fall of every realm had turned on virtue—yet from the Warring States through Qin and Han, scarcely any dynasty had endured without the sword.

sentences.zh: 夫兵豈非重事哉！

translations.literal: Ah—are arms not a weighty matter!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the business of war is no small thing!

sentences.zh: 然其因時制變，以苟利趨便，至於無所不為，而考其法制，雖可用於一時，而不足施於後世者多矣，惟唐立府兵之制，頗有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Yet in adapting to the times and altering institutions, men grasped at profit and chased convenience until there was nothing they would not do; examining their laws and systems, though many could serve for a season, few sufficed for later ages—only the Tang establishment of the fubing militia system has much worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as institutions shifted with the times, rulers chased profit and convenience until no expedient was left untried; most of their military codes served a moment but failed the ages—only the Tang fubing militia, in this regard, merits real praise.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者兵法起於井田，自周衰，王制壞而不復；

translations.literal: For in antiquity military law arose from the well-field system; from the Zhou's decline, the royal order collapsed and was not restored;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient military organization had grown out of the well-field system, but once the Zhou declined the royal order broke apart and never returned;

sentences.zh: 至於府兵，始一寓之於農，其居處、教養、畜材、待事、動作、休息，皆有節目，雖不能盡合古法，蓋得其大意焉，此高祖、太宗之所以盛也。

translations.literal: As for the fubing militia, they first lodged soldiers within farming; their dwelling, training, storing of materiel, waiting for duty, movement, and rest all had regulations—though they could not wholly accord with ancient law, they grasped its essential intent; this is why Gaozu and Taizong flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The fubing militia reunited soldiering with the soil: dwelling, training, stockpiling, waiting for call-up, marching, and rest all followed fixed rules. Though not a perfect revival of antiquity, the system captured its spirit—and therein lay the strength of Gaozu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 至其後世，子孫驕弱，不能謹守，屢變其制。

translations.literal: By later generations, their descendants grew proud and weak, unable to keep the system carefully, and changed its institutions again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Later heirs grew soft and arrogant, failed to hold the system fast, and altered it again and again.

sentences.zh: 夫置兵所以止亂，及其弊也，適足為亂，又其甚也，至困天下以養亂，而遂至於亡焉。

translations.literal: Arms are raised to stop disorder; at their worst they become disorder itself—and at the extreme the realm is exhausted to feed rebellion, until ruin follows.
translations.idiomatic: Armies exist to quell chaos, yet in decay they breed it; at the worst the whole realm is drained to sustain rebellion—and so the dynasty perishes.

sentences.zh: 蓋唐有天下二百餘年，而兵之大勢三變，其始盛時有府兵，府兵後廢而為彍騎，彍騎又廢，而方鎮之兵盛矣。

translations.literal: The Tang held the realm for more than two hundred years, and the great trend of arms changed three times: at first in its flourishing age there was the fubing militia; after the fubing militia was abolished came the Expanded Cavalry; after the Expanded Cavalry was abolished, the armies of the regional commands grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Through more than two centuries of Tang rule, military power shifted three times: first the fubing militia at the height of the dynasty; then, after its abolition, the Expanded Cavalry; and when that too failed, the regional commands rose to dominance.

sentences.zh: 及其末也，彊臣悍將兵布天下，而天子亦自置兵於京師，曰禁軍。

translations.literal: By its end, powerful ministers and fierce generals spread troops across the realm, while the Son of Heaven also established his own forces in the capital, called the Forbidden Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, strong ministers and hard generals garrisoned the empire, while the emperor maintained his own troops in the capital—the Forbidden Army.

sentences.zh: 其後天子弱，方鎮彊，而唐遂以亡滅者，措置之勢使然也。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Son of Heaven grew weak and the regional commands strong, and the Tang thus perished—the disposition of power made it so.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne weakened and the regional commands hardened, Tang fell—such was the logic of how power had been arranged.

sentences.zh: 若乃將卒、營陣、車旗、器械、征防、守衞，凡兵之事不可以悉記，記其廢置、得失、終始、治亂、興滅之迹，以為後世戒云。

translations.literal: As for generals and soldiers, encampments and formations, chariots, banners, weapons, campaigns, frontier defense, and palace guard—all matters of arms cannot be fully recorded; I record their abolition and establishment, gains and losses, beginnings and ends, order and disorder, rise and extinction, as a warning for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and ranks, camps and banners, chariots, arms, campaigns, garrisons, and guard duty—the whole apparatus of war cannot be set down in full. I record only how institutions were created and cast aside, what was gained and lost, and the arc from order to ruin, as a warning to those who come after.

sentences.zh: 府兵之制，起自西魏、後周，而備於隋，唐興因之。

translations.literal: The fubing militia system arose in Western Wei and Later Zhou, was completed in Sui, and when Tang rose it followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The fubing militia took shape under Western Wei and Later Zhou, reached full form in Sui, and Tang adopted it at the founding.

sentences.zh: 隋制十二衞，曰翊衞，曰驍騎衞，曰武衞，曰屯衞，曰禦衞，曰候衞，為左右，皆有將軍以分統諸府之兵。

translations.literal: Sui established twelve guards: Left and Right Assistants Guard, Left and Right Valiant Cavalry Guard, Left and Right Martial Guard, Left and Right Garrison Guard, Left and Right Imperial Guard, and Left and Right Outpost Guard—each with generals to divide command over the troops of the various militia districts.
translations.idiomatic: Sui organized twelve guard offices—Assistants, Valiant Cavalry, Martial, Garrison, Imperial, and Outpost guards, each in left and right wings—with generals apportioned to command the militia districts.

sentences.zh: 府有郎將、副郎將、坊主、團主，以相統治。

translations.literal: Each militia district had Commandant Lang, Deputy Commandant Lang, Ward Chiefs, and Regiment Chiefs to govern one another in hierarchy.
translations.idiomatic: Each district was ruled through Commandant Lang, Deputy Commandant Lang, ward chiefs, and regiment chiefs in descending order.

sentences.zh: 又有驃騎、車騎二府，皆有將軍。

translations.literal: There were also two offices, Fast Cavalry and Chariot Cavalry, each with its own general.
translations.idiomatic: Two headquarters oversaw them—the Fast Cavalry Office and the Chariot Cavalry Office—each headed by a general.

sentences.zh: 後更驃騎曰鷹揚郎將，車騎曰副郎將。

translations.literal: Later Fast Cavalry was renamed Hawk-Strike Commandant Lang, and Chariot Cavalry was renamed Deputy Commandant Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Fast Cavalry post became Hawk-Strike Commandant Lang and the Chariot Cavalry post Deputy Commandant Lang.

sentences.zh: 別置折衝、果毅。

translations.literal: Strike Commandant and Resolute Commandant posts were separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Commandant and Resolute Commandant ranks were added as separate offices.

sentences.zh: 自高祖初起，開大將軍府，以建成為左領大都督，領左三軍，燉煌公為右領大都督，領右三軍，元吉統中軍。

translations.literal: From Gaozu's first rise, he opened a Grand General's headquarters: Jiancheng as Left Commander-in-Chief leading the left three armies; the Duke of Dunhuang as Right Commander-in-Chief leading the right three armies; and Yuanji commanding the center army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first raised his banners, he established a grand headquarters: Jiancheng commanded the left three armies as Left Commander-in-Chief, the Duke of Dunhuang the right three as Right Commander-in-Chief, and Yuanji the center force.

sentences.zh: 發自太原，有兵三萬人。

translations.literal: Setting out from Taiyuan, he had thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Marching out of Taiyuan, he fielded thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 及諸起義以相屬與降羣盜，得兵二十萬。

translations.literal: As various uprisings joined one after another and bandit groups surrendered, he obtained two hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: As allied rebellions rallied to his cause and bandit bands submitted, his force swelled to two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 武德初，始置軍府，以驃騎、車騎兩將軍府領之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, army headquarters were first established, led by the two general offices of Fast Cavalry and Chariot Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era, army headquarters were first organized under the Fast Cavalry and Chariot Cavalry general offices.

sentences.zh: 析關中為十二道，曰：萬年道、長安道、富平道、醴泉道、同州道、華州道、寧州道、岐州道、豳州道、西麟州道、涇州道、宜州道，皆置府。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was divided into twelve circuits: Wannian, Chang'an, Fuping, Liquan, Tongzhou, Huazhou, Ningzhou, Qizhou, Binzhou, West Linzhou, Jingzhou, and Yizhou—each with a militia district established.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong region was split into twelve circuits—Wannian, Chang'an, Fuping, Liquan, Tong, Hua, Ning, Qi, Bin, West Lin, Jing, and Yi—and a militia district was placed in each.

sentences.zh: 三年，更以萬年道為參旗軍，長安道為鼓旗軍，富平道為玄戈軍，醴泉道為井鉞軍，同州道為羽林軍，華州道為騎官軍，寧州道為折威軍，岐州道為平道軍，豳州道為招搖軍，西麟州道為苑游軍，涇州道為天紀軍，宜州道為天節軍；

translations.literal: In the third year they were renamed: Wannian Circuit became the Banner of Orion Army, Chang'an Circuit the Drum-and-Banner Army, Fuping Circuit the Dark Halberd Army, Liquan Circuit the Well-Axe Army, Tongzhou Circuit the Feathered Forest Army, Huazhou Circuit the Cavalry Officer Army, Ningzhou Circuit the Breaker of Might Army, Qizhou Circuit the Level Road Army, Binzhou Circuit the Swaying Banner Army, West Linzhou Circuit the Park Excursion Army, Jingzhou Circuit the Heavenly Record Army, and Yizhou Circuit the Heavenly Node Army;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the circuits received army names: Wannian became Banner of Orion, Chang'an Drum-and-Banner, Fuping Dark Halberd, Liquan Well-Axe, Tong Feathered Forest, Hua Cavalry Officer, Ning Breaker of Might, Qi Level Road, Bin Swaying Banner, West Lin Park Excursion, Jing Heavenly Record, and Yi Heavenly Node;

sentences.zh: 軍置將、副各一人，以督耕戰，以車騎府統之。

translations.literal: Each army had one commander and one deputy to oversee farming and fighting, under the Chariot Cavalry Office.
translations.idiomatic: Each army received a commander and deputy to supervise both farming and warfare, all under the Chariot Cavalry headquarters.

sentences.zh: 六年，以天下既定，遂廢十二軍，改驃騎曰統軍，車騎曰別將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, as the realm was settled, the twelve armies were abolished; Fast Cavalry was renamed Army Commander, and Chariot Cavalry Separate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, with the realm pacified, the twelve armies were dissolved; Fast Cavalry posts became Army Commanders and Chariot Cavalry posts Separate Commanders.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，十二軍復，而軍置將軍一人，軍有坊，置主一人，以檢察戶口，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year the twelve armies were restored; each army had one general, and each army had wards with one chief to inspect households and encourage farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the twelve armies were restored; each army gained a general, and within each army wards were established with chiefs to inspect households and promote agriculture.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀十年，更號統軍為折衝都尉，別將為果毅都尉，諸府總曰折衝府。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taizong's Zhenguan reign, Army Commander was renamed Strike Commandant, Separate Commander was renamed Resolute Commandant, and all militia districts were collectively called Strike Commandant districts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 10, Taizong renamed Army Commander to Strike Commandant and Separate Commander to Resolute Commandant; all militia districts thereafter fell under the Strike Commandant system.

sentences.zh: 凡天下十道，置府六百三十四，皆有名號，而關內二百六十有一，皆以隸諸衞。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm's ten circuits, six hundred thirty-four militia districts were established, all with designations; of these, two hundred sixty-one within the Interior were all subordinate to the various guards.
translations.idiomatic: Across the ten circuits of the empire, 634 named militia districts were established; 261 within the Interior answered to the guard offices.

sentences.zh: 凡府三等：兵千二百人為上，千人為中，八百人為下。

translations.literal: Militia districts fell into three grades: twelve hundred troops for upper grade, one thousand for middle, eight hundred for lower.
translations.idiomatic: Districts ranked in three tiers: upper at 1,200 men, middle at 1,000, and lower at 800.

sentences.zh: 府置折衝都尉一人，左右果毅都尉各一人，長史、兵曹、別將各一人，校尉六人。

translations.literal: Each district had one Strike Commandant, one Left and one Right Resolute Commandant, one Chief Clerk, one Military Registrar, one Separate Commander, and six Company Captains.
translations.idiomatic: Each district was staffed by a Strike Commandant, left and right Resolute Commandants, a chief clerk, a military registrar, a separate commander, and six company captains.

sentences.zh: 士以三百人為團，團有校尉；

translations.literal: Soldiers were grouped three hundred to a regiment, each regiment with a company captain;
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred soldiers formed a regiment under a company captain;

sentences.zh: 五十人為隊，隊有正；

translations.literal: fifty to a platoon, each platoon with a squad leader;
translations.idiomatic: fifty to a platoon led by a squad chief;

sentences.zh: 十人為火，火有長。

translations.literal: ten to a fire-team, each fire-team with a chief.
translations.idiomatic: ten to a fire-team with its own chief.

sentences.zh: 火備六馱馬。

translations.literal: Each fire-team was equipped with six pack horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each fire-team maintained six pack horses.

sentences.zh: 凡火具烏布幕、鐵馬盂、布槽、鍤、钁、鑿、碓、筐、斧、鉗、鋸皆一，甲牀二，鎌二。

translations.literal: Each fire-team was furnished one black-cloth tent, iron horse basin, cloth manger, spade, hoe, chisel, mortar, basket, axe, pincers, and saw; two armor racks; and two sickles.
translations.idiomatic: Every fire-team carried one of each: black-cloth tent, iron feed basin, cloth manger, spade, hoe, chisel, mortar, basket, axe, pincers, and saw, plus two armor racks and two sickles.

sentences.zh: 隊具火鑽一，胸馬繩一，首羈、足絆皆三。

translations.literal: Each platoon had one fire-drill, one chest horse rope, and three each of head halters and leg hobbles.
translations.idiomatic: Each platoon held one fire-drill, one chest tether, and three head halters and leg hobbles apiece.

sentences.zh: 人具弓一，矢三十，胡祿、橫刀、礪石、大觿、氈帽、氈裝、行縢皆一，麥飯九斗，米二斗，皆自備，幷其介冑、戎具藏於庫。

translations.literal: Each man furnished one bow, thirty arrows, one quiver, one waist saber, one whetstone, one large awl, one felt cap, one felt kit, and one leg wrap; nine pecks of wheat meal and two pecks of rice—all self-supplied—while armor and military gear were stored in the arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier personally maintained a bow, thirty arrows, quiver, waist saber, whetstone, awl, felt cap and kit, and leg wraps, plus nine pecks of wheat and two of rice; armor and campaign gear were kept in the district storehouse.

sentences.zh: 有所征行，則視其入而出給之。

translations.literal: When there was a campaign, equipment was issued according to the number who reported.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, gear was drawn from store according to the men who mustered.

sentences.zh: 其番上宿衞者，惟給弓矢、橫刀而已。

translations.literal: Those rotating to palace guard duty received only bow, arrows, and waist saber.
translations.idiomatic: Men on rotating capital guard duty received only bow, arrows, and waist saber.

sentences.zh: 凡民年二十為兵，六十而免。

translations.literal: Commoners entered service at age twenty and were released at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners entered the rolls at twenty and were discharged at sixty.

sentences.zh: 其能騎而射者為越騎，其餘為步兵、武騎、排䂎手、步射。

translations.literal: Those able to ride and shoot became Kuaiji recruits; the rest became foot soldiers, martial cavalry, crossbow line soldiers, or foot archers.
translations.idiomatic: Men who could ride and shoot were enrolled as Kuaiji recruits; the rest served as foot soldiers, martial cavalry, crossbowmen, or foot archers.

sentences.zh: 每歲季冬，折衝都尉率五校兵馬之在府者，置左右二校尉，位相距百步。

translations.literal: Every year in late winter, the Strike Commandant led the five company captains and the troops and horses at the district, placing left and right company captains one hundred paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: Each late winter the Strike Commandant mustered the district's five company captains and available troops, posting left and right captains a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 每校為步隊十，騎隊一，皆卷矟幡，展刃旗，散立以俟。

translations.literal: Each company formed ten foot platoons and one cavalry platoon; all rolled their spear banners, unfurled bladed flags, and stood dispersed awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each wing fielded ten foot platoons and one cavalry platoon, spear banners furled and bladed flags spread, standing at loose order.

sentences.zh: 角手吹大角一通，諸校皆斂人騎為隊；

translations.literal: The horn player sounded the great horn once, and all companies gathered men and horses into platoons;
translations.idiomatic: At one blast of the great horn, every wing formed its men and horses into platoons;

sentences.zh: 二通，偃旗矟，解幡；

translations.literal: at the second blast, lowered flags and spears and unbound banners;
translations.idiomatic: at the second, lowered flags and spears and stripped the banner wrappings;

sentences.zh: 三通，旗矟舉。

translations.literal: at the third blast, raised flags and spears.
translations.idiomatic: at the third, raised flags and spears aloft.

sentences.zh: 左右校擊鼓，二校之人合譟而進。

translations.literal: Left and right companies beat drums, and the men of both wings shouted together and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right wings beat the drums and advanced together with a battle cry.

sentences.zh: 右校擊鉦，隊少却，左校進逐至右校立所；

translations.literal: The right company struck the gong; its platoons fell back slightly; the left company pressed forward in pursuit to where the right had stood;
translations.idiomatic: The right wing sounded the gong and fell back a step; the left pressed forward to the right wing's former line;

sentences.zh: 左校擊鉦，少却，右校進逐至左校立所；

translations.literal: the left company struck the gong, fell back slightly, and the right company pressed forward in pursuit to where the left had stood;
translations.idiomatic: the left wing then sounded the gong and withdrew; the right surged forward to the left wing's line;

sentences.zh: 右校復擊鉦，隊還，左校復薄戰；

translations.literal: the right company again struck the gong, platoons returned, and the left company again closed for combat;
translations.idiomatic: the right gong sounded again, platoons wheeled back, and the left closed once more for mock combat;

sentences.zh: 皆擊鉦，隊各還。

translations.literal: both struck the gong, and each platoon returned.
translations.idiomatic: both wings sounded the gong and each platoon returned to order.

sentences.zh: 大角復鳴一通，皆卷幡、攝矢、弛弓、匣刃；

translations.literal: The great horn sounded once again; all rolled banners, gathered arrows, unstrung bows, and sheathed blades;
translations.idiomatic: One more blast of the great horn: banners were furled, arrows collected, bows unstrung, and blades sheathed;

sentences.zh: 二通，旗矟舉，隊皆進；

translations.literal: at the second blast, flags and spears were raised and all platoons advanced;
translations.idiomatic: at the second, flags and spears rose and every platoon marched forward;

sentences.zh: 三通，左右校皆引還。

translations.literal: at the third blast, left and right companies all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: at the third, both wings marched back.

sentences.zh: 是日也，因縱獵，獲各入其人。

translations.literal: That same day they also held a hunt; each man kept what he caught.
translations.idiomatic: That day ended with a hunt, and each man kept his own quarry.

sentences.zh: 其隸於衞也，左、右衞皆領六十府，諸衞領五十至四十，其餘以隸東宮六率。

translations.literal: In subordination to the guards, Left and Right Guard each commanded sixty militia districts; the other guards commanded fifty down to forty; the remainder were subordinate to the Eastern Palace's six commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Under the guard system, Left and Right Guard each oversaw sixty districts, the other guards between forty and fifty, and the remainder reported to the crown prince's six commanders.

sentences.zh: 凡發府兵，皆下符契，州刺史與折衝勘契乃發。

translations.literal: Whenever fubing militia were mobilized, tally tokens were issued; only after the prefect and the Strike Commandant verified the tallies were troops dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilizing fubing militia required tally tokens; the prefect and Strike Commandant had to match them before men could march.

sentences.zh: 若全府發，則折衝都尉以下皆行；

translations.literal: If the whole district mobilized, the Strike Commandant and all below went;
translations.idiomatic: If the entire district mobilized, the Strike Commandant and all subordinates took the field;

sentences.zh: 不盡，則果毅行；

translations.literal: if not the full district, the Resolute Commandant went;
translations.idiomatic: for a partial call-up, the Resolute Commandant led;

sentences.zh: 少則別將行。

translations.literal: if fewer still, the Separate Commander went.
translations.idiomatic: for smaller detachments, the separate commander went.

sentences.zh: 當給馬者，官予其直市之，每匹予錢二萬五千。

translations.literal: Those due horses received cash from the government to purchase them—twenty-five thousand coins per horse.
translations.idiomatic: Men owed government horses received cash to buy them—twenty-five thousand coins per mount.

sentences.zh: 刺史、折衝、果毅歲閱不任戰事者鬻之，以其錢更市，不足則一府共足之。

translations.literal: Each year the prefect, Strike Commandant, and Resolute Commandant inspected and sold horses unfit for war, using the proceeds to buy replacements; if funds fell short, the whole district made up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Each year prefect, Strike Commandant, and Resolute Commandant culled unfit horses, sold them, and bought replacements; shortfalls were covered district-wide.

sentences.zh: 凡當宿衞者番上，兵部以遠近給番，五百里為五番，千里七番，一千五百里八番，二千里十番，外為十二番，皆一月上。

translations.literal: All who served palace guard rotated to the capital; the Ministry of War set rotations by distance—five hundred li: five rotations; one thousand li: seven; one thousand five hundred li: eight; two thousand li: ten; beyond that: twelve—all serving one month per rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guard duty rotated by distance set by the Ministry of War: five turns within five hundred li, seven within a thousand, eight within fifteen hundred, ten within two thousand, and twelve beyond—each turn lasting one month.

sentences.zh: 若簡留直衞者，五百里為七番，千里八番，二千里十番，外為十二番，亦月上。

translations.literal: If selected to remain on direct guard duty, five hundred li meant seven rotations, one thousand li eight, two thousand li ten, beyond that twelve—also one month per rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Men selected for extended palace guard served seven turns within five hundred li, eight within a thousand, ten within two thousand, and twelve beyond—again one month each.

sentences.zh: 先天二年誥曰：「往者分建府衞，計戶充兵，裁足周事，二十一入募，六十一出軍，多憚勞以規避匿。

translations.literal: An edict of the second year of Xiantian said: "Formerly militia districts and guards were established separately, counting households to fill the ranks—barely enough for routine duties. Men entered at twenty-one and left the army at sixty-one; many feared the labor and schemed to evade and hide.
translations.idiomatic: An Xiantian 2 edict declared: "When militia districts and guard offices were first divided and households counted to fill the ranks, the numbers barely sufficed. Entry at twenty-one and release at sixty-one bred evasion—too many men feared the burden and hid from service.

sentences.zh: 今宜取年二十五以上，五十而免。

translations.literal: Now men twenty-five and above should be taken, released at fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth enrollment should begin at twenty-five, with discharge at fifty.

sentences.zh: 屢征鎮者，十年免之。」

translations.literal: Those repeatedly sent on frontier campaigns should be exempted after ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Men repeatedly dispatched to the frontier should be released after ten years.

sentences.zh: 雖有其言，而事不克行。

translations.literal: Though these words were issued, the matter could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The decree was issued, but never put into effect.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元六年，始詔折衝府兵每六歲一簡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, an edict first ordered fubing militia of the Strike Commandant districts to be inspected every six years.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 6, Xuanzong ordered the fubing militia inspected every six years.

sentences.zh: 自高宗、武后時，天下久不用兵，府兵之法寖壞，番役更代多不以時，衞士稍稍亡匿，至是益耗散，宿衞不能給。

translations.literal: From the times of Gaozong and Empress Wu, the realm long went without war; the fubing militia law gradually decayed, rotating service was often not replaced on schedule, and guard soldiers little by little fled and hid—by now they were further scattered and depleted, and palace guard could not be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Since Gaozong and Empress Wu, long peace had rotted the fubing militia system: rotations fell out of schedule, guardsmen drifted away, and by now the rolls were so depleted that capital guard duty could no longer be filled.

sentences.zh: 宰相張說乃請一切募士宿衞。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue therefore requested that palace guard be wholly recruited from hired soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue then proposed recruiting paid soldiers for all palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 十一年，取京兆、蒲、同、岐、華府兵及白丁，而益以潞州長從兵，共十二萬，號「長從宿衞」，歲二番，命尚書左丞蕭嵩與州吏共選之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, fubing militia and common levies from Jingzhao, Pu, Tong, Qi, and Hua were taken, augmented by long-service troops from Luzhou—altogether one hundred twenty thousand—named "Long-Service Palace Guard," two rotations per year, with Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xiao Song and prefectural officials jointly selecting them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, fubing militia and common levies from Jingzhao, Pu, Tong, Qi, and Hua were combined with long-service troops from Luzhou into a force of 120,000 called the Long-Service Palace Guard, serving two rotations a year under selection by Vice Director Xiao Song and local officials.

sentences.zh: 明年，更號曰「彍騎」。

translations.literal: The next year it was renamed "Expanded Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: The following year the force was renamed the Expanded Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「諸州府馬闕，官私共補之。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Where horses are lacking in the various prefectures and militia districts, government and private parties shall jointly replenish them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered: "Where district horses ran short, public and private resources should together make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 今兵貧難致，乃給以監牧馬。」

translations.literal: Now soldiers are poor and hard pressed to obtain them, so pasture horses from the imperial stud are to be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Because soldiers were too poor to buy their own, stud horses from the imperial pastures would be issued instead.

sentences.zh: 然自是諸府士益多不補，折衝將又積歲不得遷，士人皆恥為之。

translations.literal: Yet from this time militia soldiers in the various districts increasingly failed to replenish their gear; Strike Commandant generals went years without promotion, and gentry all felt shame in the post.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, district soldiers neglected their equipment, Strike Commandants languished without promotion for years, and educated men came to regard the service as beneath them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，始以彍騎分隸十二衞，總十二萬，為六番，每衞萬人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Expanded Cavalry were first divided among the twelve guards—altogether one hundred twenty thousand, in six rotations, ten thousand men per guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Expanded Cavalry were assigned to the twelve guards: 120,000 men in six rotations, ten thousand per guard.

sentences.zh: 京兆彍騎六萬六千，華州六千，同州九千，蒲州萬二千三百，絳州三千六百，晉州千五百，岐州六千，河南府三千，陝、虢、汝、鄭、懷、汴六州各六百，內弩手六千。

translations.literal: Expanded Cavalry quotas: Jingzhao sixty-six thousand, Huazhou six thousand, Tongzhou nine thousand, Puzhou twelve thousand three hundred, Jiangzhou three thousand six hundred, Jinzhou one thousand five hundred, Qizhou six thousand, Henan Prefecture three thousand, the six prefectures of Shan, Guo, Ru, Zheng, Huai, and Bian six hundred each, and six thousand internal crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas ran: Jingzhao 66,000; Hua 6,000; Tong 9,000; Pu 12,300; Jiang 3,600; Jin 1,500; Qi 6,000; Henan 3,000; Shan, Guo, Ru, Zheng, Huai, and Bian 600 each; plus 6,000 palace crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 其制：皆擇下戶白丁、宗丁、品子彊壯五尺七寸以上，不足則兼以戶八等五尺以上，皆免征鎮、賦役。

translations.literal: The system: all selected lower-household common levies, clan youths, and sons of ranked families, sturdy and five feet seven inches or taller; if insufficient, households of the eighth rank and above five feet were also taken—all exempt from frontier garrison, taxes, and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits were drawn from lower-household commoners, clan youths, and sons of ranked families at least five feet seven inches tall; if numbers fell short, men from eighth-rank households at least five feet were included—all exempt from frontier duty, taxes, and corvée.

sentences.zh: 為四籍，兵部及州、縣、衞分掌之。

translations.literal: Four registers were kept, divided among the Ministry of War, prefectures, counties, and guards.
translations.idiomatic: Four registers were maintained, shared among the Ministry of War, prefectures, counties, and guard offices.

sentences.zh: 十人為火，五火為團，皆有首長。

translations.literal: Ten men formed a fire-team, five fire-teams a regiment—all with chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Ten men made a fire-team, five fire-teams a regiment, each with its own chief.

sentences.zh: 又擇材勇者為番頭，頗習弩射。

translations.literal: Talented and brave men were chosen as rotation chiefs, well trained in crossbow shooting.
translations.idiomatic: The bravest and most capable were made rotation chiefs, drilled especially in crossbow work.

sentences.zh: 又有羽林軍飛騎，亦習弩。

translations.literal: There were also Feathered Forest Army Flying Cavalry, likewise trained in crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: The Feathered Forest Flying Cavalry were also trained in crossbow drill.

sentences.zh: 凡伏遠弩自能施張，縱矢三百步，四發而二中；

translations.literal: For the long-range crossbow, one had to draw it unassisted, shoot three hundred paces, and hit twice in four shots;
translations.idiomatic: With the long-range crossbow, a man had to draw it alone, shoot three hundred paces, and hit twice in four shots;

sentences.zh: 擘張弩二百三十步，四發而二中；

translations.literal: with the foot-drawn crossbow, two hundred thirty paces, two hits in four shots;
translations.idiomatic: with the foot-drawn crossbow, two hundred thirty paces and two hits in four;

sentences.zh: 角弓弩二百步，四發而三中；

translations.literal: with the horn-bow crossbow, two hundred paces, three hits in four shots;
translations.idiomatic: with the horn-bow crossbow, two hundred paces and three hits in four;

sentences.zh: 單弓弩百六十步，四發而二中：皆為及第。

translations.literal: with the single-bow crossbow, one hundred sixty paces, two hits in four shots—all counted as passing.
translations.idiomatic: with the single-bow crossbow, one hundred sixty paces and two hits in four—all counted as passing the test.

sentences.zh: 諸軍皆近營為堋，士有便習者，教試之，及第者有賞。

translations.literal: All armies set up practice ranges near camp; soldiers who were adept were instructed and tested, and those who passed received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Every army maintained a practice range near camp; skilled soldiers were drilled and tested, and those who passed received rewards.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以後，彍騎之法又稍變廢，士皆失拊循。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward, the Expanded Cavalry system again gradually altered and decayed; soldiers all lost proper training and care.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era the Expanded Cavalry system slipped further into decay, and soldiers lost the discipline that had once bound them.

sentences.zh: 八載，折衝諸府至無兵可交，李林甫遂請停上下魚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Strike Commandant districts had no troops left to hand over; Li Linfu therefore requested cessation of the upper-and-lower fish tally system.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Strike Commandant districts could muster no men for transfer; Li Linfu then moved to abolish the fish-tally mobilization system.

sentences.zh: 其後徒有兵額、官吏，而戎器、馱馬、鍋幕、糗糧幷廢矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter there remained only nominal troop quotas and officials, while weapons, pack horses, kettles, tents, and dry rations were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward only paper quotas and empty offices remained; weapons, pack horses, kettles, tents, and rations were all allowed to lapse.

sentences.zh: 故時府人目番上宿衞者曰侍官，言侍衞天子；

translations.literal: In former times militia men called those rotating to palace guard "attendant officers," meaning attendants who guarded the Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Once, militia men called capital guard duty "attendant service"—service at the emperor's side;

sentences.zh: 至是，衞佐悉以假人為童奴，京師人恥之，至相罵辱必曰侍官。

translations.literal: by now guard aides all used hired men and child slaves; capital folk despised it, and when they cursed one another they always said "attendant officer."
translations.idiomatic: now guard posts were filled with hired hands and child servants; capital folk held the role in contempt, and "attendant officer" became a term of abuse.

sentences.zh: 而六軍宿衞皆市人，富者販繒綵、食粱肉，壯者為角觝、拔河、翹木、扛鐵之戲，及祿山反，皆不能受甲矣。

translations.literal: The six armies on palace guard were all marketplace men: the rich peddled silks and brocades and ate fine grain and meat; the strong performed wrestling, tug-of-war, pole-climbing, and iron-carrying games—and when Lushan rebelled, none could don armor.
translations.idiomatic: The six palace armies were staffed by townsfolk: the wealthy traded in silks and feasted on fine food; the strong amused themselves with wrestling, tug-of-war, pole-climbing, and iron-lifting—and when Lushan rose, none could bear armor.

sentences.zh: 初，府兵之置，居無事時耕於野，其番上者，宿衞京師而已。

translations.literal: At first, when the fubing militia were established, in times of peace they farmed in the fields; those on rotation served only as capital guard.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the fubing militia farmed in peacetime; only those on rotation stood guard in the capital.

sentences.zh: 若四方有事，則命將以出，事解輒罷，兵散于府，將歸于朝。

translations.literal: If trouble arose in the four directions, a general was appointed to march out; once affairs were settled the army was immediately disbanded—troops scattered to their districts, generals returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble flared, a general marched out; once it ended, the army dissolved—soldiers back to their districts, commanders back to court.

sentences.zh: 故士不失業，而將帥無握兵之重，所以防微漸、絕禍亂之萌也。

translations.literal: Thus soldiers did not lose their livelihoods, and commanders held no weight of permanent arms—the means to guard against gradual decline and cut off the sprouting of calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers kept their livelihoods; commanders never held standing armies in their grasp—the design checked small abuses before they could seed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及府兵法壞而方鎮盛，武夫悍將雖無事時，據要險，專方面，既有其土地，又有其人民，又有其甲兵，又有其財賦，以布列天下。

translations.literal: When the fubing militia law decayed and the regional commands flourished, fierce warriors and hard generals—even in peace—held strategic passes, monopolized their sectors, and possessed land, people, armor, troops, and revenue, arrayed across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fubing militia failed and regional commands rose, hard generals—even in peace—held the passes, ruled their sectors, and commanded land, people, arms, and revenue across the empire.

sentences.zh: 然則方鎮不得不彊，京師不得不弱，故曰措置之勢使然者，以此也。

translations.literal: Then the regional commands could not but grow strong and the capital could not but grow weak—thus it is said the disposition of power made it so, for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commands had to grow strong and the capital had to grow weak—this, then, is what was meant when the chronicle said the arrangement of power made Tang's fall inevitable.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂方鎮者，節度使之兵也。

translations.literal: What are called regional commands are the armies of the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commands, in essence, were the armies of the frontier commissioners.

sentences.zh: 原其始，起於邊將之屯防者。

translations.literal: Tracing its origins, it began with frontier generals' garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: In origin, it arose from the garrison defenses of frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 唐初，兵之戍邊者，大曰軍，小曰守捉，曰城，曰鎮，而總之者曰道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, troops garrisoning the frontier: the large were called armies, the small guard posts, also forts and garrisons, and what supervised them collectively was called a circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, frontier garrisons were graded: large posts were armies, smaller ones guard posts, forts, or garrisons—and the circuits that oversaw them were called dao.

sentences.zh: 若盧龍軍一，東軍等守捉十一，曰平盧道。

translations.literal: For example, one Lulong Army and eleven guard posts including Dongjun—called the Pinglu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinglu Circuit, for instance, comprised one Lulong Army and eleven guard posts such as Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 橫海、北平、高陽、經略、安塞、納降、唐興、渤海、懷柔、威武、鎮遠、靜塞、雄武、鎮安、懷遠、保定軍十六，曰范陽道。

translations.literal: Sixteen armies—Henghai, Beiping, Gaoyang, Jinglue, Ansa, Najiang, Tangxing, Bohai, Huairen, Weiwu, Zhenyuan, Jingsai, Xiongwu, Zhen'an, Huaiyuan, and Baoding—called the Fanyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang Circuit counted sixteen armies: Henghai, Beiping, Gaoyang, Jinglue, Ansa, Najiang, Tangxing, Bohai, Huairen, Weiwu, Zhenyuan, Jingsai, Xiongwu, Zhen'an, Huaiyuan, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 天兵、大同、天安、橫野軍四，岢嵐等守捉五，曰河東道。

translations.literal: Four armies—Tianbing, Datong, Tian'an, and Hengye—and five guard posts including Kelan—called the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong Circuit had four armies—Tianbing, Datong, Tian'an, and Hengye—and five guard posts including Kelan.

sentences.zh: 朔方經略、豐安、定遠、新昌、天柱、宥州經略、橫塞、天德、天安軍九，三受降、豐寧、保寧、烏延等六城，新泉守捉一，曰關內道。

translations.literal: Nine armies—Shuofang Jinglue, Feng'an, Dingyuan, Xinchang, Tianzhu, Youzhou Jinglue, Hengsai, Tiande, and Tian'an; six forts including Sanshouxiang, Fengning, Baoning, and Wuyan; one guard post at Xinquan—called the Guannei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Guannei Circuit comprised nine armies—Shuofang Jinglue, Feng'an, Dingyuan, Xinchang, Tianzhu, Youzhou Jinglue, Hengsai, Tiande, and Tian'an—six forts including Sanshouxiang, Fengning, Baoning, and Wuyan, and one guard post at Xinquan.

sentences.zh: 赤水、大斗、白亭、豆盧、墨離、建康、寧寇、玉門、伊吾、天山軍十，烏城等守捉十四，曰河西道。

translations.literal: Ten armies—Chishui, Dadou, Baiting, Doulu, Moli, Jiankang, Ningkou, Yumen, Yiwu, and Tianshan—and fourteen guard posts including Wucheng—called the Hexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi Circuit fielded ten armies—Chishui, Dadou, Baiting, Doulu, Moli, Jiankang, Ningkou, Yumen, Yiwu, and Tianshan—and fourteen guard posts including Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 瀚海、清海、靜塞軍三，沙鉢等守捉十，曰北庭道。

translations.literal: Three armies—Hanhai, Qinghai, and Jingsai—and ten guard posts including Shabo—called the Beiting Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiting Circuit had three armies—Hanhai, Qinghai, and Jingsai—and ten guard posts including Shabo.

sentences.zh: 保大軍一，鷹娑都督一，蘭城等守捉八，曰安西道。

translations.literal: One Baoda Army, one Yingsuo Protectorate, and eight guard posts including Lancheng—called the Anxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Anxi Circuit comprised one Baoda Army, one Yingsuo Protectorate, and eight guard posts including Lancheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮西、天成、振威、安人、綏戎、河源、白水、天威、榆林、臨洮、莫門、神策、寧邊、威勝、金天、武寧、曜武、積石軍十八，平夷、綏和、合川守捉三，曰隴右道。

translations.literal: Eighteen armies—Zhenxi, Tiancheng, Zhenwei, Anren, Suirong, Heyuan, Baishui, Tianwei, Yulin, Lintao, Momen, Shence, Ningbian, Weisheng, Jintian, Wuning, Yaowu, and Jishi—and three guard posts: Pingyi, Suihe, and Hechuan—called the Longyou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Longyou Circuit mustered eighteen armies—from Zhenxi and Tiancheng through Shence and Jishi—and three guard posts at Pingyi, Suihe, and Hechuan.

sentences.zh: 威戎、安夷、昆明、寧遠、洪源、通化、松當、平戎、天保、威遠軍十，，羊灌田等守捉十五，新安等城三十二，犍為等鎮三十八，曰劍南道。

translations.literal: Ten armies—Weirong, Anyi, Kunming, Ningyuan, Hongyuan, Tonghua, Songdang, Pingrong, Tianbao, and Weiyuan; fifteen guard posts including Yangguantian; thirty-two forts including Xin'an; thirty-eight garrisons including Jianwei—called the Jiannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan Circuit counted ten armies, fifteen guard posts such as Yangguantian, thirty-two forts including Xin'an, and thirty-eight garrisons including Jianwei—from Weirong and Anyi through Tianbao and Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 嶺南、安南、桂管、邕管、容管經略、清海軍六，曰嶺南道。

translations.literal: Six—Lingnan, Annan, Guiguan, Yongguan, Rongguan Jinglue, and Qinghai Army—called the Lingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingnan Circuit comprised six commands: Lingnan, Annan, Guiguan, Yongguan, Rongguan Jinglue, and the Qinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 福州經略軍一，曰江南道。

translations.literal: One Fuzhou Jinglue Army—called the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan Circuit consisted of a single Fuzhou Jinglue Army.

sentences.zh: 平海軍一，東牟、東萊守捉二，蓬萊鎮一，曰河南道。

translations.literal: One Pinghai Army, two guard posts at Dongmou and Donglai, one garrison at Penglai—called the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Circuit comprised one Pinghai Army, guard posts at Dongmou and Donglai, and a garrison at Penglai.

sentences.zh: 此自武德至天寶以前邊防之制。

translations.literal: This was the frontier defense system from the Wude era through before the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the frontier defense system from Wude down to the eve of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 其軍、城、鎮、守捉皆有使，而道有大將一人，曰大總管，已而更曰大都督。

translations.literal: Each army, fort, garrison, and guard post had a commissioner; each circuit had one great general, called Grand Commander-in-Chief, later renamed Grand Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: Every army, fort, garrison, and guard post had its commissioner; each circuit was headed by one great general, first styled Grand Commander-in-Chief and later Grand Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 至太宗時，行軍征討曰大總管，在其本道曰大都督。

translations.literal: By Taizong's time, one leading troops on campaign was called Grand Commander-in-Chief; one stationed in one's home circuit was called Grand Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, a general marching on campaign bore the title Grand Commander-in-Chief; one remaining in his home circuit was styled Grand Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 自高宗永徽以後，都督帶使持節者，始謂之節度使，然猶未以名官。

translations.literal: From Gaozong's Yonghui era onward, protector-generals who bore credentials as envoys with full discretionary powers began to be called military commissioners, though the title was not yet an official post.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's Yonghui reign, protector-generals invested with full discretionary credentials came to be called military commissioners—though the title was not yet a formal office.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，以賀拔延嗣為涼州都督、河西節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, Heluo Yansi was made Protector-General of Liangzhou and military commissioner of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2, Heluo Yansi was appointed Protector-General of Liangzhou and military commissioner of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 自此而後，接乎開元，朔方、隴右、河東、河西諸鎮，皆置節度使。

translations.literal: From then until the Kaiyuan era, the garrisons of Shuofang, Longyou, Hedong, and Hexi all received military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: From that point through Kaiyuan, the garrisons of Shuofang, Longyou, Hedong, and Hexi all received military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 及范陽節度使安祿山反，犯京師，天子之兵弱不能抗，遂陷兩京。

translations.literal: When Fanyang military commissioner An Lushan rebelled and assaulted the capital, the Son of Heaven's troops were too weak to resist, and both capitals fell.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan, military commissioner of Fanyang, rebelled and struck the capital, the emperor's own forces proved too weak to resist, and both capitals fell.

sentences.zh: 肅宗起靈武，而諸鎮之兵共起誅賊。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong rose at Lingwu, and the armies of the various garrisons together rose to execute the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong rallied at Lingwu, and the garrison armies of the realm rose together to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 其後祿山子慶緒及史思明父子繼起，中國大亂，肅宗命李光弼等討之，號「九節度之師」。

translations.literal: Later Lushan's son Qingxu and Shi Siming and his son rose in succession; the Central Plain fell into great disorder. Suzong ordered Li Guangbi and others to campaign against them—called "the Army of Nine Military Commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: Then Lushan's son Qingxu and Shi Siming and his son rose in turn, plunging the heartland into chaos; Suzong dispatched Li Guangbi and others against them in what was styled "the Army of Nine Military Commissioners."

sentences.zh: 久之，大盜既滅，而武夫戰卒以功起行陣，列為侯王者，皆除節度使。

translations.literal: After long years, once the great rebels were destroyed, fierce warriors and battle veterans who rose from the ranks by merit and were enfeoffed as marquises and kings were all appointed military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, with the great rebellion crushed, hard fighters who had risen from the ranks by merit and been enfeoffed as marquises and kings were all appointed military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 由是方鎮相望於內地，大者連州十餘，小者猶兼三四。

translations.literal: Thus regional commands lined the interior; the large ones linked more than ten prefectures, the small still held three or four.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commands now stretched across the interior: the largest linked more than ten prefectures, the smallest still held three or four.

sentences.zh: 故兵驕則逐帥，帥彊則叛上。

translations.literal: Thus when troops grew arrogant they drove out commanders; when commanders grew strong they rebelled against the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When troops grew arrogant they drove out their commanders; when commanders grew strong they rebelled against the throne.

sentences.zh: 或父死子握其兵而不肯代；

translations.literal: Sometimes when a father died the son seized his troops and refused to yield;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes a son seized his father's troops at death and refused to step aside;

sentences.zh: 或取捨由於士卒，往往自擇將吏，號為「留後」，以邀命於朝。

translations.literal: sometimes appointment and dismissal lay with the soldiers, who often chose their own officers and generals, styled "acting successors," to seek imperial confirmation from court.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes the soldiers themselves decided who would lead, choosing their own officers and generals as "acting successors" and then petitioning the court for confirmation.

sentences.zh: 天子顧力不能制，則忍恥含垢，因而撫之，謂之姑息之政。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven saw he lacked the power to control them, he swallowed shame and swallowed insult, coaxing them instead—called the policy of indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he lacked the strength to restrain them, the emperor swallowed humiliation and placated them instead—what came to be called the policy of indulgence.

sentences.zh: 蓋姑息起於兵驕，兵驕由於方鎮，姑息愈甚，而兵將愈俱驕。

translations.literal: Indulgence arose from arrogant troops; arrogant troops arose from regional commands; the more indulgence deepened, the more troops and generals alike grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Indulgence bred arrogant troops; arrogant troops arose from the regional commands; the deeper the indulgence, the more arrogant both soldiers and generals became.

sentences.zh: 由是號令自出，以相侵擊，虜其將帥，幷其土地，天子熟視不知所為，反為和解之，莫肯聽命。

translations.literal: Thereupon orders issued from themselves alone; they attacked one another, seized one another's commanders, annexed one another's territories—the Son of Heaven watched helplessly and, rather than command, mediated peace; none would heed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Orders then issued from the garrisons themselves; they raided one another, seized rival commanders, and annexed one another's lands—while the emperor looked on helplessly and played mediator rather than sovereign, and none would obey.

sentences.zh: 始時為朝廷患者，號「河朔三鎮」。

translations.literal: At first those who troubled the court were called "the Three Garrisons of Heshuo."
translations.idiomatic: At first the court's chief troublemakers were known as "the Three Garrisons of Heshuo."

sentences.zh: 及其末，朱全忠以梁兵、李克用以晉兵更犯京師，而李茂貞、韓建近據岐、華，妄一喜怒，兵已至於國門，天子為殺大臣、罪己悔過，然後去。

translations.literal: At the end, Zhu Quanzhong with Liang troops and Li Keyong with Jin troops alternately assaulted the capital; Li Maozhen and Han Jian held nearby Qishan and Huazhou—a single capricious mood and troops were already at the imperial gates; the Son of Heaven had to execute great ministers and confess his faults before they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: By the end, Zhu Quanzhong's Liang armies and Li Keyong's Jin armies alternately struck the capital, while Li Maozhen and Han Jian held Qishan and Huazhou nearby—one fit of temper and troops were at the palace gates; the emperor had to execute great ministers and confess his sins before they would withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗用崔胤召梁兵以誅宦官，劫天子奔岐，梁兵圍之逾年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong, employing Cui Yin, summoned Liang troops to execute the eunuchs, they seized the Son of Heaven and fled to Qishan; Liang troops besieged it for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong, through Cui Yin, summoned Liang troops to destroy the eunuchs, they seized the emperor and fled to Qishan, where Liang forces besieged them for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，天下之兵無復勤王者。

translations.literal: At this time, no armies in the realm still served the king with diligence.
translations.idiomatic: By then no army in the realm still marched loyally for the throne.

sentences.zh: 嚮之所謂三鎮者，徒能始禍而已。

translations.literal: Those once called the Three Garrisons could only have begun the calamity—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Garrisons of old had done no more than start the calamity.

sentences.zh: 其他大鎮，南則吳、浙、荊、湖、閩、廣，西則岐、蜀，北則燕、晉，而梁盜據其中，自國門以外，皆分裂於方鎮矣。

translations.literal: Other great garrisons: in the south Wu, Zhe, Jing, Hu, Min, and Guang; in the west Qi and Shu; in the north Yan and Jin—while the Liang usurper held the center; beyond the imperial gates all was partitioned among regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Other great garrisons held the south—Wu, Zhe, Jing, Hu, Min, and Guang—the west in Qi and Shu, the north in Yan and Jin, while the Liang usurper occupied the center; beyond the palace gates the realm was carved up among regional commands.

sentences.zh: 故兵之始重於外也，土地、民賦非天子有；

translations.literal: Thus when military power first weighed heavily outside, lands and people's levies were no longer the Son of Heaven's;
translations.idiomatic: When military power first shifted to the frontier, land and tax revenue ceased to belong to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 既其盛也，號令、征伐非其有；

translations.literal: once it flourished, orders and campaigns were no longer his;
translations.idiomatic: when it peaked, command and campaign were no longer his to give;

sentences.zh: 又其甚也，至無尺土，而不能庇其妻子宗族，遂以亡滅。

translations.literal: at its worst he possessed not even a foot of earth and could not shelter wife, children, and clan—and so perished.
translations.idiomatic: at the worst he held not a foot of soil and could not shelter wife, children, or clan—and so the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚。」

translations.literal: A saying goes: "Arms are like fire; if not kept in check they will burn the wielder."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: "Arms are like fire—leave them unchecked and they burn the hand that holds them."

sentences.zh: 夫惡危亂而欲安全者，庸君常主之能知，至於措置之失，則所謂困天下以養亂也。

translations.literal: Those who hate danger and disorder yet desire security—mediocre rulers and ordinary sovereigns can know this; but as for failures of arrangement, that is what is called exhausting the realm to nurture disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Any mediocre ruler knows to dread chaos and crave safety—but to fail in how power is arranged is to exhaust the realm feeding rebellion.

sentences.zh: 唐之置兵，既外柄以授人，而末大本小，方區區自為捍衞之計，可不哀哉！

translations.literal: Tang's disposition of troops, having surrendered outward authority to others, left the branches large and the trunk small—yet it scraped together only petty plans for self-defense; how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Tang had surrendered outward authority with its armies, leaving branches swollen and the trunk withered—yet it could manage only petty schemes of self-defense; how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 夫所謂天子禁軍者，南、北衙兵也。

translations.literal: What is called the Son of Heaven's Forbidden Army is the troops of the Southern and Northern Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's Forbidden Army, properly speaking, comprised the troops of the Southern and Northern Offices.

sentences.zh: 南衙，諸衞兵是也；

translations.literal: The Southern Office comprises the guard armies;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Office was the guard armies;

sentences.zh: 北衙者，禁軍也。

translations.literal: the Northern Office is the Forbidden Army.
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Office was the Forbidden Army.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以義兵起太原，已定天下，悉罷遣歸，其願留宿衞者三萬人。

translations.literal: At first, after Gaozu raised righteous troops at Taiyuan and had settled the realm, he disbanded and sent all home; those who wished to remain for palace guard numbered thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first raised righteous troops at Taiyuan and had pacified the realm, he disbanded the army and sent men home; thirty thousand chose to remain on palace guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖以渭北白渠旁民棄腴田分給之，號「元從禁軍」。

translations.literal: Gaozu allotted them fertile abandoned fields from commoners along the White Canal north of the Wei, styled "Original Followers Forbidden Army."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu granted them fertile abandoned fields along the White Canal north of the Wei, styling them the "Original Followers Forbidden Army."

sentences.zh: 後老不任事，以其子弟代，謂之「父子軍」。

translations.literal: Later, when the aged could no longer serve, their sons and younger kin replaced them—called the "Father-and-Son Army."
translations.idiomatic: When the veterans grew too old to serve, their sons and younger kin took their places—the "Father-and-Son Army."

sentences.zh: 及貞觀初，太宗擇善射者百人，為二番於北門長上，曰「百騎」，以從田獵。

translations.literal: By the start of Zhenguan, Taizong selected a hundred skilled archers, divided into two shifts at permanent duty north of the gate, called the "Hundred Riders," to accompany him on the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, Taizong chose a hundred expert archers, split into two shifts on standing duty north of the gate—the "Hundred Riders"—to accompany him on the hunt.

sentences.zh: 又置北衙七營，選材力驍壯，月以一營番上。

translations.literal: He also established seven Northern Office camps, selecting men of strength and daring; each month one camp rotated to palace duty.
translations.idiomatic: He also established seven Northern Office camps, drafting the strong and bold; each month one camp rotated to palace duty.

sentences.zh: 十二年，始置左右屯營於玄武門，領以諸衞將軍，號「飛騎」。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he first established Left and Right Garrison Camps at the Xuanwu Gate, led by guard generals, styled the "Flying Riders."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he first established Left and Right Garrison Camps at the Xuanwu Gate under guard generals, styled the "Flying Riders."

sentences.zh: 其法：取戶二等以上、長六尺闊壯者，試弓馬四次上、翹關舉五、負米五斛行三十步者。

translations.literal: The method: take households of the second rank and above, men six feet tall and broad-built, who passed bow and horse at the fourth degree or better, who could lift the gate bar five times, and who could carry five hu of grain thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: The standard: households of the second rank and above, men six feet tall and broad-shouldered, who scored fourth class or better in bow and horsemanship, could lift the gate bar five times, and carry five hu of grain thirty paces.

sentences.zh: 復擇馬射為百騎，衣五色袍，乘六閑駁馬，虎皮韉，為游幸翊衞。

translations.literal: From these he again chose mounted archers for the Hundred Riders, clad in robes of five colors, riding piebald horses from the six royal studs with tiger-skin saddles, to escort the emperor on tours.
translations.idiomatic: From these he chose mounted archers for the Hundred Riders, clad in robes of five colors, riding piebald horses from the imperial studs with tiger-skin saddles, to escort the emperor on progress.

sentences.zh: 高宗龍朔二年，始取府兵越騎、步射置左右羽林軍，大朝會則執仗以衞階陛，行幸則夾馳道為內仗。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 of Gaozong, fubing crossbow cavalry and foot archers were first taken to establish the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies; at great court assemblies they bore arms to guard the steps and dais; on imperial progress they flanked the imperial roadway as inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Longshuo 2, fubing crossbow cavalry and foot archers were formed into the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies; at great court assemblies they bore arms to guard the steps, and on imperial progress they flanked the roadway as the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 武后改百騎曰「千騎」。

translations.literal: Empress Wu renamed the Hundred Riders the "Thousand Riders."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu renamed the Hundred Riders the "Thousand Riders."

sentences.zh: 中宗又改千騎曰「萬騎」，分左、右營。

translations.literal: Zhongzong again renamed the Thousand Riders the "Ten Thousand Riders," divided into Left and Right camps.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong renamed them again—the "Ten Thousand Riders"—split into Left and Right camps.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗以萬騎平韋氏，改為左右龍武軍，皆用唐元功臣子弟，制若宿衞兵。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong with the Ten Thousand Riders quelled the Wei clan, he renamed them the Left and Right Dragon Martial Armies, all drawn from sons and younger kin of founding Tang meritorious officials, regulated like palace guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong used the Ten Thousand Riders to crush the Wei clan, he reorganized them as the Left and Right Dragon Martial Armies, staffed with sons and younger kin of Tang's founding meritorious officials under the same rules as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 是時，良家子避征戍者，亦皆納資隸軍，分日更上如羽林。

translations.literal: At that time, sons of good families seeking to avoid frontier garrison duty also paid fees to enroll in the armies, rotating day by day on duty like the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Then sons of good families seeking to evade frontier service paid fees to enroll, rotating on duty day by day like the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，詔左右羽林軍、飛騎闕，取京旁州府士，以戶部印印其臂，為二籍，羽林、兵部分掌之。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan 12: when vacancies arose in the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies and Flying Riders, men were taken from prefectures near the capital; the Revenue Ministry stamped their arms with its seal; two registers were kept, the Feathered Forest and War Ministry each holding one.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12, when the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies and Flying Riders had vacancies, men were drawn from prefectures near the capital; the Revenue Ministry stamped their arms with its seal, and two registers were kept, one held by the Feathered Forest and one by the War Ministry.

sentences.zh: 末年，禁兵寖耗，及祿山反，天子西駕，禁軍從者裁千人，肅宗赴靈武，士不滿百，及即位，稍復調補北軍。

translations.literal: In late years the Forbidden Army gradually dwindled; when Lushan rebelled the Son of Heaven fled west—fewer than a thousand Forbidden troops followed; Suzong reached Lingwu with fewer than a hundred men; after enthronement he gradually restored and replenished the Northern Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's late years the Forbidden Army dwindled; when Lushan rebelled the emperor fled west with fewer than a thousand guards, and Suzong reached Lingwu with fewer than a hundred men—only after enthronement did he gradually restore and replenish the Northern Armies.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，置左右神武軍，補元從、扈從官子弟，不足則取它色，帶品者同四軍，亦曰「神武天騎」，制如羽林。

translations.literal: Zhide 2: Left and Right Divine Martial Armies were established, filled with sons of original followers and escort officials; if insufficient, others were taken—those bearing rank same as the four armies; also called "Divine Martial Heavenly Riders," regulated like the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 the Left and Right Divine Martial Armies were established, filled first with sons of original followers and escort officials, then with others if need be—ranked men treated like the four armies; also called the "Divine Martial Heavenly Riders," under Feathered Forest regulations.

sentences.zh: 總曰「北衙六軍」。

translations.literal: Collectively called the "Six Armies of the Northern Office."
translations.idiomatic: Together they were called the "Six Armies of the Northern Office."

sentences.zh: 又擇便騎射者置衙前射生手千人，亦曰「供奉射生官」，又曰「殿前射生」，分左、右廂，總號曰「左右英武軍」。

translations.literal: Skilled mounted archers were again selected—a thousand bowmen before the office, also called "Palace Service Bowmen," also "Hall Bowmen," divided into Left and Right wings—collectively styled the "Left and Right Heroic Martial Armies."
translations.idiomatic: A thousand skilled mounted archers were also chosen as bowmen before the office—styled "Palace Service Bowmen" or "Hall Bowmen," split into Left and Right wings and collectively called the "Left and Right Heroic Martial Armies."

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，李輔國用事，請選羽林騎士五百人徼巡。

translations.literal: Qianyuan 1: Li Fuguo held power and requested five hundred Feathered Forest cavalrymen for patrol.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1, Li Fuguo, then dominant at court, requested five hundred Feathered Forest cavalry for patrol duty.

sentences.zh: 李揆曰：「漢以南、北軍相制，故周勃以北軍安劉氏。

translations.literal: Li Kui said: "Han used Southern and Northern Armies to check each other; thus Zhou Bo secured the Liu house through the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui objected: "Han balanced Southern and Northern Armies against each other—thus Zhou Bo saved the Liu house through the Northern Army.

sentences.zh: 朝廷置南、北衙，文武區列，以相察伺。

translations.literal: The court placed Southern and Northern Offices, civil and military separately arrayed, to watch one another.
translations.idiomatic: Our court set up Southern and Northern Offices, civil and military kept apart, to watch one another.

sentences.zh: 今用羽林代金吾警，忽有非常，何以制之？」

translations.literal: Now employing Feathered Forest in place of the Jinwu guard—if sudden crisis arises, by what means will they be controlled?"
translations.idiomatic: If Feathered Forest replaces the Jinwu guard, what check remains when sudden crisis strikes?"

sentences.zh: 遂罷。

translations.literal: The proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上元中，以北衙軍使衞伯玉為神策軍節度使，鎮陝州，中使魚朝恩為觀軍容使，監其軍。

translations.literal: During Shangyuan, Northern Office army commander Wei Boyu was made military commissioner of the Shence Army, garrisoned at Shaanzhou; palace envoy Yu Chao'en was made army-inspection commissioner to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era, Northern Office commander Wei Boyu was made military commissioner of the Shence Army at Shaanzhou, while palace envoy Yu Chao'en was appointed army-inspection commissioner to supervise it.

sentences.zh: 初，哥舒翰破吐蕃臨洮西之磨環川，即其地置神策軍，以成如璆為軍使。

translations.literal: At first, after Geshu Han defeated the Tibetans at Mohuan River west of Lintao, he established the Shence Army on that ground, with Cheng Ruyou as army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, after Geshu Han defeated the Tibetans at Mohuan River west of Lintao, he established the Shence Army there under Cheng Ruyou as army commander.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，如璆以伯玉將兵千人赴難，伯玉與朝恩皆屯于陝。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Ruyou led a thousand troops under Boyu to the throne's aid; Boyu and Chao'en both encamped at Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Ruyou marched a thousand men under Boyu to the throne's aid; Boyu and Chao'en both encamped at Shaan.

sentences.zh: 時邊土陷蹙，神策故地淪沒，即詔伯玉所部兵，號「神策軍」，以伯玉為節度使，與陝州節度使郭英乂皆鎮陝。

translations.literal: Frontier lands were then collapsing inward; the Shence Army's original territory was lost—thereupon Boyu's command was decreed the "Shence Army," Boyu made military commissioner, he and Shaanzhou commissioner Guo Yingyi both garrisoned Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: As the frontier collapsed and the Shence Army's original territory was lost, Boyu's command was decreed the "Shence Army," with Boyu as military commissioner; he and Shaanzhou commissioner Guo Yingyi both garrisoned Shaan.

sentences.zh: 其後伯玉罷，以英乂兼神策軍節度。

translations.literal: Later Boyu was dismissed and Yingyi additionally held command of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later Boyu was dismissed, and Yingyi additionally took command of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 英乂入為僕射，軍遂統於觀軍容使。

translations.literal: When Yingyi entered court as Vice Director, the army came under the army-inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingyi entered court as Vice Director, the army passed to the army-inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，以射生軍入禁中清難，皆賜名「寶應功臣」，故射生軍又號「寶應軍」。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended, bowmen entered the inner palace to purge disorder and were all granted the title "Baoying Meritorious Officials"; hence the bowmen were also called the "Baoying Army."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended, bowmen entered the inner palace to quell disorder and were all granted the title "Baoying Meritorious Officials"—hence the bowmen were also called the "Baoying Army."

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，代宗避吐蕃幸陝，朝恩舉在陝兵與神策軍迎扈，悉號「神策軍」。

translations.literal: Guangde 1: Daizong, fleeing the Tibetans, visited Shaan; Chao'en led all troops at Shaan and the Shence Army to receive and escort him—all styled "Shence Army."
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1, Daizong fled the Tibetans to Shaan; Chao'en led all troops there and the Shence Army to receive and escort him—all styled "Shence Army."

sentences.zh: 天子幸其營。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven visited their camp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited their camp.

sentences.zh: 及京師平，朝恩遂以軍歸禁中，自將之，然尚未與北軍齒也。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, Chao'en brought the army back into the inner palace and commanded it himself—yet it was not yet ranked with the Northern Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was restored, Chao'en brought the army into the inner palace and commanded it himself—yet it was not yet ranked with the Northern Armies.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，吐蕃復入寇，朝恩又以神策軍屯苑中，自是寖盛，分為左、右廂，勢居北軍右，遂為天子禁軍，非它軍比。

translations.literal: Yongtai 1: Tibetans invaded again; Chao'en again garrisoned the Shence Army in the imperial park—from then it gradually flourished, split into Left and Right wings, its power ranking above the Northern Armies, and became the Son of Heaven's Forbidden Army, unlike any other force.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 the Tibetans invaded again; Chao'en garrisoned the Shence Army in the imperial park—from then it grew steadily, split into Left and Right wings, outranked the Northern Armies, and became the emperor's own Forbidden Army, unlike any other force.

sentences.zh: 朝恩乃以觀軍容宣慰處置使知神策軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: Chao'en then held the posts of army-inspection commissioner, pacification commissioner, and disposal commissioner, and also served as Shence Army troop commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en then combined the posts of army-inspection, pacification, and disposal commissioner with command of Shence Army troops.

sentences.zh: 大曆四年，請以京兆之好畤，鳳翔之麟游、普潤，皆隸神策軍。

translations.literal: Dali 4: he requested that Hao of Jingzhao, and Linyou and Purun of Fengxiang all be placed under the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 4 he requested that Hao in Jingzhao and Linyou and Purun in Fengxiang all be placed under the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以興平、武功、扶風、天興隸之，朝廷不能遏。

translations.literal: The next year Xingping, Wugong, Fufeng, and Tianxing were also placed under it—the court could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xingping, Wugong, Fufeng, and Tianxing were added as well—and the court could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 又用愛將劉希暹為神策虞候，主不法，遂置北軍獄，募坊市不逞，誣捕大姓，沒產為賞，至有選舉旅寓而挾厚貲多橫死者。

translations.literal: He also employed his favorite Liu Xixuan as Shence Army adjutant in charge of law enforcement, set up a Northern Army prison, recruited ruffians from the market wards, falsely arrested great clans, confiscated property as reward—until men traveling for the civil examinations, lodging abroad with great wealth, were often killed by violence.
translations.idiomatic: He also placed his favorite Liu Xixuan in charge of Shence law enforcement, set up a Northern Army prison, recruited market ruffians, falsely arrested great clans, and confiscated property as reward—until examination candidates lodging abroad with large fortunes were often murdered.

sentences.zh: 朝恩得罪死，以希暹代為神策軍使。

translations.literal: When Chao'en was condemned and executed, Xixuan replaced him as Shence Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao'en was condemned and executed, Xixuan replaced him as Shence Army commander.

sentences.zh: 是歲，希暹復得罪，以朝恩舊校王駕鶴代將。

translations.literal: That year Xixuan was again condemned; Chao'en's former subordinate Wang Jiahe replaced him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xixuan was condemned in turn; Chao'en's former subordinate Wang Jiahe took command.

sentences.zh: 十數歲，德宗即位，以白志貞代之。

translations.literal: A dozen years later, when Dezong ascended, Bai Zhibei replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a decade later, when Dezong ascended, Bai Zhibei replaced him.

sentences.zh: 是時，神策兵雖處內，而多以裨將將兵征伐，往往有功。

translations.literal: At this time, though the Shence Army was stationed within, many of its deputy commanders led troops on campaign and often won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Shence Army was stationed within the capital, many of its deputy commanders led troops on campaign and often won distinction.

sentences.zh: 及李希烈反，河北盜且起，數出禁軍征伐，神策之士多鬬死者。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled and bandits in Hebei also rose, the Forbidden Army was repeatedly sent on campaign; many Shence soldiers died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled and banditry flared in Hebei, the Forbidden Army was sent out again and again, and many Shence soldiers fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 建中四年下詔募兵，以志貞為使，蒐補峻切。

translations.literal: Jianzhong 4 an edict summoned recruits; Zhibei was made commissioner—recruitment was harsh and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4 an edict called for recruits; Zhibei was made commissioner, and recruitment was harsh and relentless.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀之婿端王傅吳仲孺殖貲累巨萬，以國家有急不自安，請以子率奴馬從軍。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's son-in-law, Tutor to the Prince of Duan Wu Zhongru, amassed wealth of tens of thousands—uneasy at the realm's emergency, he offered his son leading slaves and horses to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's son-in-law Wu Zhongru, tutor to the Prince of Duan, had amassed wealth in the tens of thousands; troubled by the national emergency, he offered his son with slaves and horses for service.

sentences.zh: 德宗喜甚，為官其子五品。

translations.literal: Dezong was greatly pleased and granted his son a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was delighted and granted his son a fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 志貞乃請節度、都團練、觀察使與世嘗任者家，皆出子弟馬奴裝鎧助征，授官如仲孺子。

translations.literal: Zhibei then requested that families of military commissioners, regimental trainers, and inspection commissioners who had once held office should all send out sons, horses, slaves, armor, and equipment to aid the campaign—offices granted as with Zhongru's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibei then requested that families of military commissioners, regimental trainers, and inspection commissioners who had once held office send sons, horses, slaves, armor, and equipment to aid the campaign—offices granted as with Zhongru's son.

sentences.zh: 於是豪富者緣為幸，而貧者苦之。

translations.literal: The wealthy seized the chance for fortune; the poor suffered.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy seized the opportunity for gain; the poor bore the burden.

sentences.zh: 神策兵既發殆盡，志貞陰以市人補之，名隸籍而身居市肆。

translations.literal: Once Shence troops were nearly all deployed, Zhibei secretly filled rolls with townsfolk—enrolled in name but dwelling in shops.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shence troops were nearly all deployed, Zhibei secretly filled the rolls with townsfolk—listed on the registers but living in their shops.

sentences.zh: 及涇卒潰變，皆戢伏不出，帝遂出奔。

translations.literal: When the Jingzhou garrison mutinied and collapsed, all cowered and would not emerge—the Emperor fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingzhou garrison mutinied, all cowered and refused to emerge—and the emperor fled.

sentences.zh: 初，段秀實見禁兵寡弱，不足備非常，上疏曰：「天子萬乘，諸侯千，大夫百，蓋以大制小，十制一也，尊君卑臣彊幹弱支之道。

translations.literal: At first, Duan Xiushi saw the Forbidden Army weak and few, insufficient against sudden crisis, and memorialized: "The Son of Heaven commands ten thousand chariots, feudal lords a thousand, grand masters a hundred—this is using the large to control the small, ten to control one: the way of honoring the ruler, lowering ministers, strengthening the trunk, and weakening the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Duan Xiushi, seeing the Forbidden Army weak and too few for sudden crisis, memorialized: "The Son of Heaven commands ten thousand chariots, feudal lords a thousand, grandees a hundred—using the large to govern the small, ten to govern one: the way of honoring the ruler, humbling ministers, strengthening the trunk, and weakening the branches.

sentences.zh: 今外有不廷之虜，內有梗命之臣，而禁兵不精，其數削少，後有猝故，何以待之？

translations.literal: Now without are unsubmissive barbarians; within are ministers who defy orders—yet the Forbidden Army is unskilled and its numbers dwindling; if sudden crisis comes, how shall it be met?
translations.idiomatic: Now unsubmissive barbarians press from without and defiant ministers from within—yet the Forbidden Army is unskilled and dwindling; if sudden crisis strikes, how will we meet it?

sentences.zh: 猛虎所以百獸畏者，爪牙也，爪牙廢，則孤豚特犬悉能為敵。

translations.literal: The tiger is feared by all beasts because of claws and fangs; once claws and fangs are ruined, even a lone piglet or stray dog can be its foe.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger is feared because of its claws and fangs—ruin those, and even a lone piglet or stray dog can stand against it.

sentences.zh: 願少留意。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to give this some heed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to give this some heed.

sentences.zh: 至是方以秀實言為然。

translations.literal: Only then did [the emperor] finally deem Xiushi's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the court finally concede that Xiushi had been right.

sentences.zh: 及志貞等流貶，神策都虞候李晟與其軍之它將，皆自飛狐道西兵赴難，遂為神策行營節度，屯渭北，軍遂振。

translations.literal: When Zhibei and the others were exiled, Shence acting commandant Li Sheng and other generals of the army all led troops west via Flying Fox Road to relieve the crisis; he was made commander of the Shence field command, encamped north of the Wei River, and the army was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhibei and his allies were exiled, Shence acting commandant Li Sheng and other Shence generals marched west through Flying Fox Pass to save the throne. Li Sheng was made commander of the Shence field army, encamped north of the Wei, and the army regained its vigor.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，改神策左右廂為左右神策軍，特置監句當左右神策軍，以寵中官，而益置大將軍以下。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan 2: the Left and Right Shence wings were renamed the Left and Right Shence Armies; supervisors were specially appointed to oversee the Left and Right Shence Armies, to favor eunuchs, and ranks from Great General downward were further added.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 the Left and Right Shence wings became the Left and Right Shence Armies. Supervisors were specially appointed to run them—a favor to eunuchs—and more ranks were added below Great General.

sentences.zh: 又改殿前射生左右廂曰殿前左右射生軍，亦置大將軍以下。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Archer wings before the hall were also renamed the Left and Right Hall Archer Armies, and Great General and below were likewise established.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Hall Archer wings were renamed the Left and Right Hall Archer Armies, with Great General and lower ranks likewise established.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔射生、神策、六軍將士，府縣以事辦治，先奏乃移軍，勿輒逮捕。

translations.literal: Year 3: an edict ordered that for archer, Shence, and Six Armies officers and soldiers, when prefectures and counties handled cases they must report first before transferring [cases] to the army—do not rashly arrest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ruled that when prefectures and counties dealt with archer, Shence, or Six Armies personnel, they must report first and only then refer the case to the army—not arrest on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹鄭叔則建言：「京劇輕猾所聚，慝作不常，俟奏報，將失罪人，請非昏田，皆以時捕。」

translations.literal: Jingzhao governor Zheng Shuzhe proposed: "The capital gathers the frivolous and slippery; wicked acts are incessant—wait for memorial and reply and criminals will be lost. I ask that except on the eve of the plowing rite, all may be arrested in season.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao governor Zheng Shuzhe proposed: "The capital is thick with rogues and tricksters, and villainy never rests. If we wait for memorial and reply, offenders will escape. I ask that arrests be made promptly on every day save that of the royal plowing rite.

sentences.zh: 乃可之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 俄改殿前左右射生軍曰左右神策威軍，置監左右神威軍使。

translations.literal: Soon the Left and Right Hall Archer Armies were renamed the Left and Right Divine Prestige Armies, and supervisors of the Left and Right Divine Prestige Armies were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Left and Right Hall Archer Armies were renamed the Left and Right Divine Prestige Armies, with supervisors appointed for each.

sentences.zh: 左右神策軍皆加將軍二員，左右龍武軍加將軍一員，以待諸道大將有功者。

translations.literal: Two general slots were added to each Left and Right Shence Army, one to each Left and Right Dragon Martial Army, to accommodate meritorious frontier generals.
