translations.idiomatic: Two generalships were added to each Shence Army and one to each Dragon Martial Army, reserved for meritorious generals from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 自肅宗以後，北軍增置威武、長興等軍，名類頗多，而廢置不一。

translations.literal: From Suzong onward the Northern Army added Armies such as Martial Prestige and Everlasting Prosperity—many names and titles, abolished and established without uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong the Northern Armies proliferated—Martial Prestige, Everlasting Prosperity, and many other names—created and abolished without fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 惟羽林、龍武、神武、神策、神威最盛，總曰左右十軍矣。

translations.literal: Only the Feathered Forest, Dragon Martial, Divine Martial, Shence, and Divine Prestige were strongest—in all, the Left and Right Ten Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Only Feathered Forest, Dragon Martial, Divine Martial, Shence, and Divine Prestige remained strongest—the Left and Right Ten Armies in all.

sentences.zh: 其後京畿之西，多以神策軍鎮之，皆有屯營。

translations.literal: Thereafter west of the capital region the Shence Army garrisoned many posts, each with encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Shence troops garrisoned much of the western capital region, each post with its own camp.

sentences.zh: 軍司之人，散處甸內，皆恃勢凌暴，民間苦之。

translations.literal: Army officials scattered throughout the capital districts all relied on power to bully and oppress—the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Shence officials posted across the capital districts bullied the populace by force, to the people's great distress.

sentences.zh: 自德宗幸梁還，以神策兵有勞，皆號「興元元從奉天定難功臣」，恕死罪。

translations.literal: From Dezong's return after visiting Liang, because the Shence soldiers had served with merit, all were styled "Meritorious Followers from Xingyuan Who Settled the Crisis at Fengtian," pardoned capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: After Dezong's return from Fengtian, every Shence soldier who had marched with him was styled "Original Follower from Xingyuan Who Settled the Crisis at Fengtian," with capital crimes remitted.

sentences.zh: 中書、御史府、兵部乃不能歲比其籍，京兆又不敢總舉名實。

translations.literal: The Secretariat, Censorate, and Ministry of War could not annually verify their registers; Jingzhao again did not dare fully tally names against reality.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, Censorate, and War Ministry could no longer keep annual rosters current, and the Jingzhao governor did not dare reconcile names with actual men.

sentences.zh: 三輔人假比於軍，一牒至十數。

translations.literal: People of the Three Adjuncts falsely enrolled in the armies—one man up to a dozen certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the Three Adjuncts took false army enrollment—one person might hold as many as ten or more certificates.

sentences.zh: 長安姦人多寓占兩軍，身不宿衞，以錢代行，謂之納課戶。

translations.literal: Many Chang'an miscreants nominally enrolled in both armies, never overnight on guard, paying money in lieu of service—called "fee-paying households."
translations.idiomatic: Many Chang'an rascals held nominal slots in both armies without ever standing guard, paying cash for substitutes—these were called "fee-paying households."

sentences.zh: 益肆為暴，吏稍禁之，輒先得罪，故當時京尹、赤令皆為之斂屈。

translations.literal: They grew even more violent; when officials slightly restrained them, the officials were punished first—so then the capital governor and county magistrates all drew back in deference.
translations.idiomatic: They grew bolder still in violence; any official who curbed them was punished first—so capital governors and magistrates learned to hold their tongues.

sentences.zh: 十年，京兆尹楊於陵請置挾名敕，五丁許二丁居軍，餘差以條限，繇是豪彊少畏。

translations.literal: Year 10: Jingzhao governor Yang Yuling requested an edict against false enrollment—of five men two might serve in the army, the rest assigned by statute—whereupon powerful families were somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Jingzhao governor Yang Yuling secured an edict against false enrollment: of every five men only two might remain in the army, the rest reassigned by statute—and the great clans grew somewhat wary.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以監句當左神策軍、左監門衞大將軍、知內侍省事竇文場為左神策軍護軍中尉，監句當右神策軍、右監門衞將軍、知內侍省事霍仙鳴為右神策軍護軍中尉，監右神威軍使、內侍兼內謁者監張尚進為右神威軍中護軍，監左神威軍使、內侍兼內謁者監焦希望為左神威軍中護軍。

translations.literal: Year 12: Dou Wenchang, supervisor of the Left Shence Army, Left Gate Guard Great General, and director of the Palace Domestic Service, was made Left Shence Army protecting-army vice-commandant; Huo Xianming, supervisor of the Right Shence Army, Right Gate Guard general, and director of the Palace Domestic Service, was made Right Shence Army protecting-army vice-commandant; Zhang Shangjin, supervisor of the Right Divine Prestige Army, palace eunuch and director of Inner Admittedly Affairs, was made Right Divine Prestige Army mid-protecting general; Jiao Xiwang, supervisor of the Left Divine Prestige Army, palace eunuch and director of Inner Admittedly Affairs, was made Left Divine Prestige Army mid-protecting general.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Dou Wenchang—supervisor of the Left Shence Army, Left Gate Guard Great General, and head of the Palace Domestic Service—was made Left Shence protecting-army vice-commander; Huo Xianming, his counterpart on the right, became Right Shence protecting-army vice-commander; Zhang Shangjin, supervisor of the Right Divine Prestige Army, became its mid-protector; and Jiao Xiwang, supervisor of the Left Divine Prestige Army, became its mid-protector.

sentences.zh: 護軍中尉、中護軍皆古官，帝既以禁衞假宦官，又以此寵之。

translations.literal: Protecting-army vice-commandant and mid-protecting general were both ancient offices; the emperor, having entrusted the Forbidden Guard to eunuchs, further favored them with these titles.
translations.idiomatic: Protecting-army vice-commander and mid-protector were ancient titles; having put the Forbidden Guard in eunuch hands, the emperor now lavished these honors on them as well.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又詔左右神策置統軍，以崇親衞，如六軍。

translations.literal: Year 14: an edict further ordered the Left and Right Shence to establish army commanders, to elevate the imperial guard, like the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Left and Right Shence Armies were ordered to establish supreme commanders, elevating them to match the Six Armies as imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 時邊兵衣饟多不贍，而戍卒屯防，藥茗蔬醬之給最厚。

translations.literal: At the time frontier soldiers' clothing and provisions were often insufficient, while garrison troops on static defense received the thickest allotments of medicine, tea, vegetables, and sauce.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops often lacked clothing and rations, yet static garrison soldiers received the richest supplies of medicine, tea, vegetables, and condiments.

sentences.zh: 諸將務為詭辭，請遙隸神策軍，稟賜遂贏舊三倍，繇是塞上往往稱神策行營，皆內統於中人矣，其軍乃至十五萬。

translations.literal: Generals contrived pretexts to petition distant attachment to the Shence Army; stipends and gifts then exceeded the old rate threefold—whereupon borderlands often called themselves Shence field commands, all internally governed by eunuchs; the army reached a hundred and fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Generals contrived to have their units nominally placed under the Shence Army; pay and gifts then tripled. Border commands began calling themselves Shence field armies, all answerable inward to eunuchs—and the Shence rolls swelled to 150,000 men.

sentences.zh: 故事，京城諸司、諸使、府、縣，皆季以御史巡囚。

translations.literal: By precedent, all offices, agencies, prefectures, and counties of the capital were quarterly inspected by censors reviewing prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: By custom censors quarterly inspected prisoners held by every capital office, agency, prefecture, and county.

sentences.zh: 後以北軍地密，未嘗至。

translations.literal: Later, because Northern Army precincts were restricted, [censors] never went there.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Northern Army quarters were deemed too sensitive, and censors never entered.

sentences.zh: 十九年，監察御史崔薳不知近事，遂入右神策，中尉奏之，帝怒，杖薳四十，流崖州。

translations.literal: Year 19: Supervising censor Cui Wan, unaware of recent practice, entered the Right Shence Army; the vice-commandant memorialized; the emperor was angered, had Wan beaten forty strokes, and exiled him to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year supervising censor Cui Wan, unaware of the new rules, entered the Right Shence camp. The vice-commander reported it; the emperor had Wan beaten forty strokes and exiled to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，王叔文用事，欲取神策兵柄，乃用故將范希朝為左右神策、京西諸城鎮行營兵馬節度使，以奪宦者權而不克。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, Wang Shuwen held power, sought the Shence military command, and appointed the former general Fan Xichao commander of the Left and Right Shence and Western Capital garrison field army—seeking to wrest authority from eunuchs but failing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended, Wang Shuwen tried to seize the Shence command and named the veteran Fan Xichao commander of the Left and Right Shence and the western capital garrisons—but could not pry power from the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，省神武軍。

translations.literal: Yuanhe 2: the Divine Martial Army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2 the Divine Martial Army was abolished.

sentences.zh: 明年，又廢左右神威軍，合為一，曰「天威軍」。

translations.literal: The next year the Left and Right Divine Prestige Armies were abolished and merged into one called "Heavenly Prestige Army."
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Left and Right Divine Prestige Armies were merged into a single Heavenly Prestige Army.

sentences.zh: 八年，廢天威軍，以其兵騎分隸左右神策軍。

translations.literal: Year 8: Heavenly Prestige was abolished; its infantry and cavalry were divided between the Left and Right Shence Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Heavenly Prestige was abolished and its troops divided between the Left and Right Shence Armies.

sentences.zh: 及僖宗幸蜀，田令孜募神策新軍為五十四都，離為十軍，令孜自為左右神策十軍兼十二衞觀軍容使，以左右神策大將軍為左右神策諸都指揮使，諸都又領以都將，亦曰「都頭」。

translations.literal: When Xizong fled to Shu, Tian Lingze recruited new Shence troops into fifty-four companies divided into ten armies. Lingze made himself commander of the Left and Right Shence Ten Armies and concurrently commissioner overseeing the Twelve Guards; the Shence great generals became supreme commanders of the Shence companies; each company was further led by a company chief, also called "company head."
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong fled to Shu, Tian Lingze raised new Shence forces in fifty-four companies under ten armies. Lingze became commander of the Left and Right Shence Ten Armies and commissioner over the Twelve Guards; Shence great generals became supreme commanders of the companies, each company led by a company chief—the "company heads."

sentences.zh: 景福二年，昭宗以藩臣跋扈、天子孤弱，議以宗室典禁兵。

translations.literal: Jingfu 2: Zhaozong, seeing frontier lords overbearing and the Son of Heaven isolated, deliberated putting imperial clan members in charge of the Forbidden Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingfu 2, with warlords defiant and the throne isolated, Zhaozong considered placing princes of the blood over the Forbidden Army.

sentences.zh: 及伐李茂貞，乃用嗣覃王允為京西招討使，神策諸都指揮使李鐬副之，悉發五十四軍屯興平，已而兵自潰，茂貞逼京師，昭宗為斬神策中尉西門重遂、李周𧬤，乃引去。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Li Maozhen, he appointed Prince Yun, the Situ Prince, western-capital pacification commissioner, with Shence supreme commander Li Wei as deputy; all fifty-four armies encamped at Xingping—but soon the troops dispersed on their own. Maozhen pressed the capital; Zhaozong executed Shence vice-commanders Ximen Zhongsui and Li Zhoubian; Maozhen then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Li Maozhen, he named Prince Yun, the Situ Prince, western-capital pacification commissioner, with Shence supreme commander Li Wei as deputy, and sent all fifty-four armies to Xingping—but they soon melted away. Maozhen pressed the capital; Zhaozong executed Shence vice-commanders Ximen Zhongsui and Li Zhoubian; only then did Maozhen withdraw.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，王行瑜、韓建及茂貞連兵犯闕，天子又殺宰相韋昭度、李磎，乃去。

translations.literal: Qianning 1: Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Maozhen jointly marched on the capital; the Son of Heaven again executed chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Jiao; they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 1, Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Maozhen marched on the capital together; the emperor executed chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Jiao; only then did they withdraw.

sentences.zh: 太原李克用以其兵伐行瑜等，同州節度使王行實入迫神策中尉駱全瓘、劉景宣請天子幸邠州，全瓘、景宣及子繼晟與行實縱火東市，帝御承天門，敕諸王率禁軍扞之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong of Taiyuan marched against Xingyu and the others. Tongzhou governor Wang Xingshi entered the capital and pressed Shence vice-commanders Luo Quanhong and Liu Jingxuan to ask the Son of Heaven to visit Binzhou. Quanhong, Jingxuan, and Jingxuan's son Jicheng with Xingshi set fire to the Eastern Market. The emperor mounted the Chengtian Gate and ordered the princes to lead the Forbidden Army to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Taiyuan marched against Xingyu and his allies. Tongzhou governor Wang Xingshi entered the capital and, with Shence vice-commanders Luo Quanhong and Liu Jingxuan, pressed the emperor to flee to Binzhou. Quanhong, Jingxuan, Jingxuan's son Jicheng, and Xingshi torched the Eastern Market. The emperor took the Chengtian Gate and ordered the princes to lead the Forbidden Army against them.

sentences.zh: 捧日都頭李筠以其軍衞樓下，茂貞將閻圭攻筠，矢及樓扉，帝乃與親王、公主幸筠軍，扈蹕都頭李君實亦以兵至，侍帝出幸莎城、石門。

translations.literal: Holding-the-Sun company head Li Yun with his troops guarded below the tower; Maozhen's general Yan Gui attacked Yun—the arrows reached the tower doors. The emperor then went with princes and princesses to Yun's army; escort company head Li Junshi also arrived with troops, attending the emperor's departure to Shacheng and Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Holding-the-Sun company head Li Yun posted his men below the gate tower. Maozhen's general Yan Gui attacked him; arrows struck the tower doors. The emperor fled with princes and princesses to Yun's camp; escort company head Li Junshi arrived with troops and accompanied the emperor to Shacheng and Shimen.

sentences.zh: 詔嗣薛王知柔入長安收禁軍、清宮室，月餘乃還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Zhirou, the Situ Prince, to enter Chang'an, gather the Forbidden Army, and clear the palace halls—returning only after more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong ordered Prince Zhirou into Chang'an to rally the Forbidden Army and restore the palace—a month passed before he returned.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸王閱親軍，收拾神策亡散，得數萬。

translations.literal: An edict further ordered the princes to review the imperial guard and gather scattered Shence troops—several tens of thousands were found.
translations.idiomatic: The princes were ordered to review the imperial guard and gather scattered Shence soldiers—recovering tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 益置安聖、捧宸、保寧、安化軍，曰「殿後四軍」，嗣覃王允與嗣延王戒丕將之。

translations.literal: Four armies were further established—Ansheng, Holding-the-Court, Protecting Tranquility, and Pacifying Transformation—called "the Four Rear Hall Armies," commanded by Prince Yun the Situ and Prince Jiepi the Yanting.
translations.idiomatic: Four new armies were raised—Tranquil Sage, Upholding the Throne, Guarding Tranquility, and Pacifying the Realm—the "Four Rear Hall Armies," under Princes Yun and Jiepi.

sentences.zh: 三年，茂貞再犯闕，嗣覃王戰敗，昭宗幸華州。

translations.literal: Year 3: Maozhen again marched on the capital; the Situ Prince was defeated; Zhaozong fled to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Maozhen attacked the capital again; Prince Yun was beaten; Zhaozong fled to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，韓建畏諸王有兵，請皆歸十六宅，留殿後兵三十人，為控鶴排馬官，隸飛龍坊，餘悉散之，且列甲圍行宮，於是四軍二萬餘人皆罷。

translations.literal: The next year Han Jian, fearing the princes with troops, requested all return to the Sixteen Mansions; thirty Rear Hall troops remained as crane-controlling and horse-ranking officers under Flying Dragon Ward—the rest were all dispersed, and armored columns encircled the mobile palace—whereupon all forty-some thousand of the Four Armies were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Han Jian, fearing armed princes, had them all confined to the Sixteen Mansions. Thirty Rear Hall soldiers remained as crane handlers and horse stewards under Flying Dragon Ward; the rest were disbanded, and armored columns ringed the mobile palace—more than twenty thousand men of the Four Armies were gone.

sentences.zh: 又請誅都頭李筠，帝恐，為斬於大雲橋。

translations.literal: He further asked execution of company head Li Yun; the emperor, in fear, had Yun beheaded at Dayun Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian also demanded the death of company head Li Yun; terrified, the emperor had him executed at Dayun Bridge.

sentences.zh: 俄遂殺十一王。

translations.literal: Soon eleven princes were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon eleven princes were murdered.

sentences.zh: 及還長安，左右神策軍復稍置之，以六千人為定。

translations.literal: When [the emperor] returned to Chang'an, the Left and Right Shence Armies were gradually reestablished at a fixed six thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an the Left and Right Shence Armies were slowly rebuilt—a fixed strength of six thousand.

sentences.zh: 是歲，左右神策中尉劉季述、王仲先以其兵千人廢帝，幽之。

translations.literal: That year Left and Right Shence vice-commanders Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian with a thousand troops deposed the emperor and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shence vice-commanders Liu Jishu and Wang Zhongxian used a thousand troops to depose the emperor and confine him.

sentences.zh: 季述等誅。

translations.literal: Jishu and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu and his conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 已而昭宗召朱全忠兵入誅宦官，宦官覺，劫天子幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Soon Zhaozong summoned Zhu Quanzhong's troops to enter and execute the eunuchs; the eunuchs realized it, seized the Son of Heaven, and carried him to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong then summoned Zhu Quanzhong's army to slaughter the eunuchs; the eunuchs caught wind, seized the emperor, and fled with him to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 全忠圍之歲餘，天子乃誅中尉韓全誨、張弘彥等二十餘人，以解梁兵，乃還長安。

translations.literal: Quanzhong besieged more than a year; the Son of Heaven then executed vice-commanders Han Quanhui, Zhang Hongyan, and more than twenty others to relieve the Liang army; then returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang for over a year until the emperor executed vice-commanders Han Quanhui, Zhang Hongyan, and twenty-odd others to appease the Liang forces—then returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 於是悉誅宦官，而神策左右軍繇此廢矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon all eunuchs were executed—and the Left and Right Shence Armies were abolished from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every eunuch was killed, and with them the Left and Right Shence Armies were abolished for good.

sentences.zh: 諸司悉歸尚書省郎官，兩軍兵皆隸六軍，而以崔胤判六軍十二衞事。

translations.literal: All offices returned entirely to Secretariat directorate officials; both armies' soldiers all came under the Six Armies, with Cui Yin adjudicating Six Armies and Twelve Guards affairs.
translations.idiomatic: All offices reverted to Secretariat officials; both armies' troops passed to the Six Armies, with Cui Yin overseeing the Six Armies and Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 六軍者，左右龍武、神武、羽林，其名存而已。

translations.literal: The Six Armies—Left and Right Dragon Martial, Divine Martial, and Feathered Forest—existed in name only.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies—Dragon Martial, Divine Martial, and Feathered Forest, left and right—survived in name alone.

sentences.zh: 自是軍司以宰相領。

translations.literal: From then the army command was led by the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth a chancellor headed the army administration.

sentences.zh: 及全忠歸，留步騎萬人屯故兩軍，以子友倫為左右軍宿衞都指揮使，禁衞皆汴卒。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong returned, he left ten thousand infantry and cavalry garrisoned at the former two armies' posts; his son Youlun was made overnight guard supreme commander of the Left and Right Armies—the Forbidden Guard were all Bian troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong left, he stationed ten thousand infantry and cavalry in the old Shence barracks and made his son Youlun supreme commander of the palace guard—all Bianzhou men now.

sentences.zh: 崔胤乃奏：「六軍名存而兵亡，非所以壯京師。

translations.literal: Cui Yin then memorialized: "The Six Armies exist in name but their troops are gone—this cannot strengthen the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin memorialized: "The Six Armies are names without soldiers—hardly a strong capital defense.

sentences.zh: 軍皆置步軍四將，騎軍一將。

translations.literal: Each army should establish four infantry generals and one cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: Each army should have four infantry commanders and one cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 步將皆兵二百五十人，騎將皆百人，總六千六百人。

translations.literal: Each infantry general commands two hundred fifty men, each cavalry general one hundred—in all six thousand six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each infantry commander would hold 250 men, each cavalry commander 100—6,600 in all.

sentences.zh: 番上如故事。」

translations.literal: Rotation to palace duty as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Palace rotation would follow the old schedule.

sentences.zh: 乃令六軍諸衞副使京兆尹鄭元規立格募兵於市，而全忠陰以汴人應之。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Six Armies and Guard deputy commander, Jingzhao governor Zheng Yuangui, to recruit soldiers in the market by fixed standards—but Quanzhong secretly had Bian men answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies deputy and Jingzhao governor Zheng Yuangui were ordered to recruit in the markets—but Quanzhong quietly filled the rolls with men from Bian.

sentences.zh: 胤死，以宰相裴樞判左三軍，獨孤損判右三軍，向所募士悉散去。

translations.literal: When Yin died, chancellor Pei Shu adjudicated the Left Three Armies and Dugu Sun the Right Three Armies; the recently recruited soldiers all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin's death Pei Shu took the Left Three Armies and Dugu Sun the Right Three; every recruit melted away.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦兼判左右六軍十二衞。

translations.literal: Quanzhong also concurrently adjudicated the Left and Right Six Armies and Twelve Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong himself assumed control of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards.

sentences.zh: 及東遷，唯小黃門打毬供奉十數人、內園小兒五百人從。

translations.literal: When they moved east, only a dozen or so junior eunuchs serving as polo attendants and five hundred Inner Garden boys followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the forced move east, only a dozen junior polo eunuchs and five hundred Inner Garden pages accompanied the court.

sentences.zh: 至穀水，又盡屠之，易以汴人，於是天子無一人之衞。

translations.literal: Reaching Gushui, all were slaughtered and replaced with Bian men—whereupon the Son of Heaven had not a single man of his own guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushui they were massacred and swapped for Bianzhou soldiers—the emperor left without a single guardsman of his own.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遇弒，唐乃亡。

translations.literal: Zhaozong was assassinated; Tang then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong was murdered—and Tang fell.

sentences.zh: 馬者，兵之用也；

translations.literal: Horses are the tools of war;
translations.idiomatic: Horses are the instruments of war;

sentences.zh: 監牧，所以蕃馬也，其制起於近世。

translations.literal: Pasturage supervision is how horses are bred; the system arose in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturage supervision exists to breed horses—a system of relatively recent origin.

sentences.zh: 唐之初起，得突厥馬二千匹，又得隋馬三千於赤岸澤，徙之隴右，監牧之制始於此。

translations.literal: When Tang first rose it obtained two thousand Turkish horses and three thousand Sui horses at Red Bank Marsh, moved them to Longyou—pasturage supervision began here.
translations.idiomatic: At its founding Tang acquired 2,000 Göktürk horses and 3,000 Sui horses from Red Bank Marsh, moved them to Longyou, and the pasturage system began.

sentences.zh: 其官領以太僕；

translations.literal: Its chief official was the Court of the Imperial Stud;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Stud headed it;

sentences.zh: 其屬有牧監、副監；

translations.literal: under it were pasturage directors and deputy directors;
translations.idiomatic: beneath it were pasturage directors and deputy directors;

sentences.zh: 監有丞，有主簿、直司、團官、牧尉、排馬、牧長、羣頭，有正，有副；

translations.literal: Each directorate had an aide, registrar, direct clerk, herd officials, pasturage captains, horse-ranking officers, herd chiefs, and group heads, each with principal and deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Each directorate had aides, registrars, clerks, herd officers, pasturage captains, horse-rankers, herd chiefs, and group heads—principal and deputy for each;

sentences.zh: 凡羣置長一人，十五長置尉一人，歲課功，進排馬。

translations.literal: Each herd had one chief; for every fifteen chiefs one captain was appointed; annually achievements were assessed and horse-rankers promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Every herd had one chief; one captain for every fifteen chiefs; yearly assessments determined promotions to horse-ranker.

sentences.zh: 又有掌閑，調馬習上。

translations.literal: There were also handlers of the stables, training horses for mounting.
translations.idiomatic: Stable masters trained horses for imperial riding.

sentences.zh: 又以尚乘掌天子之御。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Mount also managed the Son of Heaven's personal steeds.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Imperial Mount managed the emperor's personal horses.

sentences.zh: 左右六閑：一曰飛黃，二曰吉良，三曰龍媒，四曰騊駼，五曰駃騠，六曰天苑。

translations.literal: Left and Right Six Stables: first Flying Yellow, second Auspicious Fine, third Dragon Matchmaker, fourth Taotu, fifth Jueti, sixth Heavenly Park.
translations.idiomatic: Six stables on left and right: Flying Yellow, Auspicious Fine, Dragon Matchmaker, Taotu, Jueti, and Heavenly Park.

sentences.zh: 總十有二閑為二廄，一曰祥驎，二曰鳳苑，以繫飼之。

translations.literal: Twelve stables in all formed two studs: first Auspicious Unicorn, second Phoenix Park, where they were tethered and fed.
translations.idiomatic: All twelve were grouped into two imperial studs—Auspicious Unicorn and Phoenix Park—where horses were stabled and fed.

sentences.zh: 其後禁中又增置飛龍廄。

translations.literal: Later the Forbidden City further added Flying Dragon Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Later the inner palace added the Flying Dragon Stud.

sentences.zh: 初，用太僕少卿張萬歲領羣牧。

translations.literal: At first Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Zhang Wansui oversaw the herd pasturages.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Vice Minister Zhang Wansui of the Imperial Stud oversaw the herd pasturages.

sentences.zh: 自貞觀至麟德四十年間，馬七十萬六千，置八坊岐、豳、涇、寧間，地廣千里，一曰保樂，二曰甘露，三曰南普閏，四曰北普閏，五曰岐陽，六曰太平，七曰宜祿，八曰安定。

translations.literal: From Zhenguan to Linde, forty years—706,000 horses; eight pastures were established between Qi, Bin, Jing, and Ning—land a thousand li wide: first Protecting Joy, second Sweet Dew, third South Puchang, fourth North Puchang, fifth Qiyang, sixth Great Peace, seventh Yilu, eighth Anding.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenguan through Linde—forty years—the herds reached 706,000 horses. Eight pastures were laid out across Qi, Bin, Jing, and Ning, a thousand li of land: Protecting Joy, Sweet Dew, South Puchang, North Puchang, Qiyang, Great Peace, Yilu, and Anding.

sentences.zh: 八坊之田，千二百三十頃，募民耕之，以給芻秣。

translations.literal: The eight pastures' fields—1,230 qing—were worked by recruited commoners to supply fodder.
translations.idiomatic: 1,230 qing of pasture land were farmed by hired peasants to supply fodder.

sentences.zh: 八坊之馬為四十八監，而馬多地狹不能容，又析八監列布河西豐曠之野。

translations.literal: The eight pastures' horses formed forty-eight directorates; but horses were many and land narrow and could not contain them—eight directorates were further divided and spread across the rich open country west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The eight pastures supported forty-eight directorates, but land grew scarce; eight more were split off across the broad pastures west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 凡馬五千為上監，三千為中監，餘為下監。

translations.literal: Five thousand horses made a superior directorate, three thousand a middle directorate, the remainder inferior directorates.
translations.idiomatic: 5,000 horses marked a superior directorate, 3,000 a middle one, fewer a subordinate one.

sentences.zh: 監皆有左、右，因地為之名。

translations.literal: Each directorate had left and right [branches], named according to local terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Each directorate had left and right branches, named for their terrain.

sentences.zh: 方其時，天下以一縑易一馬。

translations.literal: At that time throughout the realm one bolt of silk traded for one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were so plentiful that one bolt of silk bought a horse empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 萬歲掌馬久，恩信行於隴右。

translations.literal: Wansui long managed horses; grace and trust extended across Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui's long stewardship won loyalty throughout Longyou.

sentences.zh: 後以太僕少卿鮮于匡俗檢校隴右牧監。

translations.literal: Later Vice Minister Xianyu Kuangsuh was appointed acting Longyou pasturage director.
translations.idiomatic: Later Vice Minister Xianyu Kuangsuh was made acting director of Longyou pasturage.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，以太僕少卿李思文檢校隴右諸牧監使，監牧有使自是始。

translations.literal: During Yifeng, Vice Minister Li Siwen was appointed acting commissioner of Longyou pasturage directorates—from this the pasturage commissioner began.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng era Li Siwen became acting commissioner over Longyou pasturage—creating the pasturage commissioner post.

sentences.zh: 後又有羣牧都使，有閑廄使，使皆置副，有判官。

translations.literal: Later there was also a supreme herd commissioner and an imperial stud commissioner; each commissioner had deputies and adjudicating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later came a supreme herd commissioner and an imperial stud commissioner, each with deputies and adjudicators.

sentences.zh: 又立四使：南使十五，西使十六，北使七，東使九。

translations.literal: Four commissioners were further established: Southern fifteen, Western sixteen, Northern seven, Eastern nine.
translations.idiomatic: Four regional commissioners were added—Southern (15), Western (16), Northern (7), Eastern (9).

sentences.zh: 諸坊若涇川、亭川、闕水、洛、赤城，南使統之；

translations.literal: Pastures such as Jingchuan, Tingchuan, Queshui, Luo, and Chicheng were governed by the Southern commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Pastures such as Jingchuan, Tingchuan, Queshui, Luo, and Chicheng fell under the Southern commissioner;

sentences.zh: 清泉、溫泉，西使統之；

translations.literal: Qingquan and Wenquan were governed by the Western commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Qingquan and Wenquan fell under the Western commissioner;

sentences.zh: 烏氏，北使統之；

translations.literal: Wushi was governed by the Northern commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Wushi fell under the Northern commissioner;

sentences.zh: 木硤、萬福，東使統之。

translations.literal: Muqia and Wanfu were governed by the Eastern commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Muqia and Wanfu fell under the Eastern commissioner.

sentences.zh: 它皆失傳。

translations.literal: The rest are lost and untransmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Other details have been lost.

sentences.zh: 其後益置八監於鹽州，三監於嵐州。

translations.literal: Later eight directorates were added at Yanzhou and three at Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later eight directorates were added at Yan and three at Lan.

sentences.zh: 鹽州使八，統白馬等坊；

translations.literal: The eight Yanzhou commissioners governed pastures such as White Horse;
translations.idiomatic: Eight Yan commissioners oversaw pastures including White Horse;

sentences.zh: 嵐州使三，統樓煩、玄池、天池之監。

translations.literal: the three Lanzhou commissioners governed the directorates of Loufan, Dark Pool, and Heaven Pool.
translations.idiomatic: three Lan commissioners oversaw Loufan, Dark Pool, and Heaven Pool.

sentences.zh: 凡征伐而發牧馬，先盡彊壯，不足則取其次。

translations.literal: Whenever campaigning drew on stud horses, the strongest and stoutest were taken first; if insufficient, the next grade was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign requisitions took the strongest stallions first, then lesser stock if needed.

sentences.zh: 錄色、歲、膚第印記、主名送軍，以帳馱之，數上於省。

translations.literal: Color, age, hide grade, brand-mark, and owner's name were recorded and sent to the army, carried on ledger sheets, counts reported upward to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Each horse's color, age, hide grade, brand, and owner were logged, ledgered for dispatch, and tallies sent to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 自萬歲失職，馬政頗廢，永隆中，夏州牧馬之死失者十八萬四千九百九十。

translations.literal: From Wansui's loss of office, horse administration greatly declined; in Yonglong, horses dead or lost at Xiazhou pasturage totaled 184,990.
translations.idiomatic: After Wansui fell from power horse policy collapsed; in Yonglong Xiazhou pasturage reported 184,990 horses dead or missing.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，詔羣牧歲出高品，御史按察之。

translations.literal: Jingyun 2: an edict ordered yearly delivery of high-grade horses from the herds, inspected by censors.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 herds were ordered to deliver top-grade horses yearly, with censor inspection.

sentences.zh: 開元初，國馬益耗，太常少卿姜晦乃請以空名告身市馬於六胡州，率三十匹讎一游擊將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, state horses grew ever more depleted; Vice Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Hui then requested to purchase horses in the Six Hu Prefectures with blank commission certificates, at a rate of thirty horses exchanged for one Guerrilla General commission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign state horse stocks dwindled further. Vice Minister of Ceremonies Jiang Hui proposed buying horses from the Six Hu Prefectures with blank rank commissions—thirty horses for one Guerrilla General appointment.

sentences.zh: 命王毛仲領內外閑廄。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhong was ordered to oversee the inner and outer stud farms.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhong was put in charge of the inner and outer imperial studs.

sentences.zh: 九年又詔：「天下之有馬者，州縣皆先以郵遞軍旅之役，定戶復緣以升之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year another edict declared: "All in the realm who possessed horses—in every prefecture and county they were first assigned postal relay and military corvee duties, and registered households were moreover advanced in rank on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year another edict declared: "Anyone in the empire who kept horses found prefectures and counties assigning them first to postal relay and military service, while registered households were also moved up in category because of it.

sentences.zh: 百姓畏苦，乃多不畜馬，故騎射之士減曩時。

translations.literal: The common people feared the hardship and largely ceased keeping horses, so mounted archers were fewer than in former times.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners dreaded the burden and largely stopped raising horses, and cavalrymen became far fewer than before.

sentences.zh: 自今諸州民勿限有無蔭，能家畜十馬以上，免帖驛郵遞征行，定戶無以馬為貲。」

translations.literal: From now on commoners in all prefectures shall not be limited by whether they enjoy inherited privilege; those who can keep ten horses or more at home are exempt from relay and postal requisition duties, and registered households will not count horses as taxable assets.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth commoners in every prefecture, regardless of inherited privilege, who kept ten or more horses at home would be exempt from relay and courier requisitions, and horses would no longer count as household wealth for registration.

sentences.zh: 毛仲既領閑廄，馬稍稍復，始二十四萬，至十三年乃四十三萬。

translations.literal: Maozhong having taken charge of the stud farms, horses gradually recovered—at first 240,000, and by the thirteenth year 430,000.
translations.idiomatic: Once Maozhong took over the studs, horse numbers slowly recovered: 240,000 at first, and 430,000 by the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥款塞，玄宗厚撫之，歲許朔方軍西受降城為互市，以金帛市馬，於河東、朔方、隴右牧之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Turks submitted to the border; Emperor Xuanzong treated them generously, and each year allowed the Shuo Fang Army's West Shouxiang City as a trade market, purchasing horses with gold and silk and pasturing them in Hedong, Shuo Fang, and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Turks came in submission; Xuanzong treated them generously and each year opened West Shouxiang City of the Shuo Fang Army as a horse market, buying mounts with gold and silk and grazing them across Hedong, Shuo Fang, and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 既雜胡種，馬乃益壯。

translations.literal: Having mixed in foreign breeds, the horses grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbred with foreign stock, the horses grew notably stronger.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，諸軍戰馬動以萬計。

translations.literal: After the Tianbao era, campaign horses in the various armies often numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianbao, each army's war horses routinely ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 王侯、將相、外戚牛駝羊馬之牧布諸道，百倍於縣官，皆以封邑號名為印自別；

translations.literal: Princes, marquises, generals, ministers, and consort kin had pastures of cattle, camels, sheep, and horses spread across the circuits, a hundred times more than the government, all using their fief titles as seal names to distinguish themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Princes, generals, ministers, and imperial in-laws pastured cattle, camels, sheep, and horses across the circuits in numbers a hundred times the government's, each branding herds with their fief names;

sentences.zh: 將校亦備私馬。

translations.literal: commanders and officers also maintained private horses.
translations.idiomatic: officers and commanders kept private mounts as well.

sentences.zh: 議謂秦、漢以來，唐馬最盛，天子又銳志武事，遂弱西北蕃。

translations.literal: Commentary held that since Qin and Han, Tang horses were most abundant; the Son of Heaven also keenly pursued military affairs, and thus weakened the northwestern frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said that since Qin and Han no dynasty had matched Tang horse power; the emperor's keen martial ambition had in turn weakened the northwestern tribes.

sentences.zh: 十一載，詔二京旁五百里勿置私牧。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of the era, an edict forbade establishing private pastures within five hundred li of the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year an edict banned private pasturage within five hundred li of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 十三載，隴右羣牧都使奏：馬牛駝羊總六十萬五千六百，而馬三十二萬五千七百。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Longyou Herd Commissioner General reported: horses, cattle, camels, and sheep totaled 605,600, of which horses were 325,700.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Longyou Herd Commissioner General reported 605,600 head of horses, cattle, camels, and sheep altogether, including 325,700 horses.

sentences.zh: 安祿山以內外閑廄都使兼知樓煩監，陰選勝甲馬歸范陽，故其兵力傾天下而卒反。

translations.literal: An Lushan, as Commissioner of the Inner and Outer Stud Farms and concurrently managing the Loufan Directorate, secretly selected the finest armored horses for Fanyang; thus his military power dominated the realm and he finally rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan held the post of Commissioner of the Inner and Outer Studs while also overseeing Loufan Directorate; he secretly funneled the best armored horses to Fanyang, building a force that overshadowed the empire until he rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 肅宗收兵至彭原，率官吏馬抵平涼，蒐監牧及私羣，得馬數萬，軍遂振。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong gathered troops at Pengyuan, led official and civil horses to Pingliang, searched stud farms and private herds, obtained tens of thousands of horses, and the army was thereby revived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong rallied troops at Pengyuan, drove official and civilian horses to Pingliang, and scoured stud farms and private herds for tens of thousands of mounts, reviving the army.

sentences.zh: 至鳳翔，又詔公卿百寮以後乘助軍。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Fengxiang, he again ordered the high ministers and all officials to contribute spare mounts to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang he ordered ministers and officials to donate their spare horses to the war effort.

sentences.zh: 其後邊無重兵，吐蕃乘隙陷隴右，苑牧畜馬皆沒矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter the frontier lacked heavy garrisons; the Tibetans seized the opportunity and captured Longyou, and all pasture and stud horses were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with no strong frontier garrison, Tibet seized the opening and overran Longyou, and every stud and pasture horse was lost.

sentences.zh: 乾元後，回紇恃功，歲入馬取繒，馬皆病弱不可用。

translations.literal: After Qianyuan, the Uighurs relied on their merits, each year bringing horses to receive silk; the horses were all sickly, weak, and unusable.
translations.idiomatic: After Qianyuan the Uighurs, trading on their wartime service, brought horses yearly for silk tribute—but the animals were sickly and useless.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，代宗欲親擊虜，魚朝恩乃請大搜城中百官、士庶馬輸官，曰「團練馬」。

translations.literal: Yongtai 1: Emperor Daizong wished to strike the enemy in person; Yu Chaoen then requested a sweeping search of horses belonging to officials and commoners in the city to be surrendered to the government, called "drill-training horses."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1, when Daizong planned to lead a personal strike against the enemy, Yu Chaoen proposed a citywide sweep to seize horses from officials and commoners for the state as "drill-training mounts."

sentences.zh: 下制禁馬出城者，已而復罷。

translations.literal: An edict was issued forbidding horses to leave the city; soon afterward it was repealed.
translations.idiomatic: An order banning horses from leaving the city was issued, then quickly withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 德宗建中元年，市關輔馬三萬實內廄。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, Jianzhong 1: 30,000 horses were purchased in the capital region to fill the inner stud.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's first Jianzhong year, thirty thousand horses were bought in the capital region to restock the inner stud.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，吐蕃、羌、渾犯塞，詔禁大馬出潼、蒲、武關者。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan 3: Tibetans, Qiang, and Hun raided the border; an edict forbade large horses to pass out through Tong, Pu, and Wu passes.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3, with Tibetans, Qiang, and Hun raiding the frontier, an edict barred large horses from leaving through Tong, Pu, and Wu passes.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年伐蔡，命中使以絹二萬市馬河曲。

translations.literal: Yuanhe 11, campaigning against Cai: a palace envoy was ordered to purchase horses at Hequ with twenty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe 11 campaign against Cai, a palace envoy was sent to buy horses at Hequ with twenty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其始置四十八監也，據隴西、金城、平涼、天水，員廣千里，繇京度隴，置八坊為會計都領，其間善水草腴田皆隸之。

translations.literal: When the forty-eight directorates were first established, they occupied Longxi, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui over an area more than a thousand li wide; from the capital crossing Long, eight pastures were set as accounting headquarters, and all good grass, water, and fertile fields within were subordinated to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the forty-eight directorates were first established they sprawled across Longxi, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui for more than a thousand li; eight pastures west of the capital beyond Long served as accounting hubs, and every tract of good pasture and fertile land fell under them.

sentences.zh: 後監牧使與坊皆廢，故地存者一歸閑廄，旋以給貧民及軍吏，間又賜佛寺、道館幾千頃。

translations.literal: Later the herd commissioners and pastures were all abolished; surviving land briefly returned to the stud farms, then was soon granted to poor commoners and military clerks, and in between was also bestowed on Buddhist temples and Daoist abbeys in thousands of qing.
translations.idiomatic: Later the herd commissioners and pastures were abolished; remaining land briefly reverted to the studs, then passed to poor commoners and army clerks, with thousands of qing also granted to temples and Daoist abbeys.

sentences.zh: 十二年，閑廄使張茂宗舉故事，盡收岐陽坊地，民失業者甚衆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Stud Commissioner Zhang Maozong cited precedent and recovered all Qiyang pasture land; very many people lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Stud Commissioner Zhang Maozong invoked precedent and reclaimed all Qiyang pasture land, leaving large numbers of people without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以蔡州牧地為龍陂監。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Caizhou pasture land was made the Longpo Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Caizhou pasture land became the Longpo Directorate.

sentences.zh: 十四年，置臨漢監於襄州，牧馬三千二百，費田四百頃。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Linhan Directorate was established at Xiangzhou, pasturing 3,200 horses at a cost of 400 qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Linhan Directorate was set up at Xiangzhou with 3,200 horses, consuming four hundred qing of land.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，岐人叩闕訟茂宗所奪田，事下御史按治，悉予民。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, people of Qi petitioned at the palace gates over land seized by Maozong; the matter was referred to censors for investigation, and all was returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, Qi residents petitioned at court over land Maozong had seized; censors investigated and returned it all to the people.

sentences.zh: 大和七年，度支鹽鐵使言：「銀州水甘草豐，請詔刺史劉源市馬三千，河西置銀川監，以源為使。」

translations.literal: Dahe 7: the Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau reported: "Yinzhou has abundant water and rich grass; we request an edict ordering Prefect Liu Yuan to purchase three thousand horses, establish the Yinchuan Directorate west of the Yellow River, and appoint Yuan as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 7 the Salt and Iron Commissioner reported: "Yinzhou has plentiful water and grass; we ask that Prefect Liu Yuan be ordered to buy three thousand horses, that a Yinchuan Directorate be established west of the river, and that Yuan be made its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 襄陽節度使裴度奏停臨漢監。

translations.literal: Xiangyang Military Commissioner Pei Du memorialized to halt the Linhan Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang Jiedushi Pei Du memorialized to abolish the Linhan Directorate.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，劉源奏：「銀川馬已七千，若水草乏，則徙牧綏州境。

translations.literal: Kaicheng 2: Liu Yuan memorialized: "Yinchuan horses already number seven thousand; if grass and water run short, they should be transferred to graze in Suizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 2 Liu Yuan reported: "Yinchuan already holds seven thousand horses; if pasture runs short, they should be moved to graze in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 今綏南二百里，四隅險絕，寇路不能通，以數十人守要，畜牧無它患。」

translations.literal: Now two hundred li south of Suizhou, the four corners are perilously enclosed; enemy routes cannot pass through, and with several dozen men guarding the passes, herding has no other worries.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li south of Suizhou the terrain is enclosed on every side; no enemy route can reach it, and a few dozen men at the passes would suffice to herd without further risk.

sentences.zh: 乃以隸銀川監。

translations.literal: It was then made subordinate to the Yinchuan Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The area was then placed under the Yinchuan Directorate.

sentences.zh: 其後闕，不復可紀。

translations.literal: Thereafter records are missing and can no longer be chronicled.
translations.idiomatic: After that the record breaks off and can no longer be traced.
